problem_statement: OpenFermion needs a bosonic symbolic operator type so users can represent bosonic ladder-operator expressions directly and ask basic structural questions about whether those expressions are already in bosonic normal order or preserve boson number.
requirements: Provide a BosonOperator symbolic operator type for bosonic ladder-operator terms.
Allow BosonOperator instances to recognize bosonic normal ordering, including empty operators, number operators, and reversed creation-annihilation orderings.
Allow BosonOperator instances to report whether every term preserves boson number, independent of the term ordering within each bosonic ladder sequence.
Keep the existing FermionOperator normal-ordering behavior unchanged.

interface.Name: BosonOperator
interface.Description: Represents bosonic ladder-operator expressions as a SymbolicOperator subclass.

interface.Name: BosonOperatorError
interface.Description: Exception type exposed by the BosonOperator module for bosonic-operator validation and parsing failures.

interface.Name: is_normal_ordered
interface.Description: Returns whether every term is in bosonic normal order.

interface.Name: is_boson_preserving
interface.Description: Returns whether every term preserves the total boson number.

problem_statement: OpenFermion should support freezing occupied and unoccupied orbitals directly on a FermionOperator so users can form active-space Hamiltonians from second-quantized operators while preserving the correct fermionic signs and removing gaps in the remaining orbital numbering.
requirements: Provide a freeze_orbitals helper for FermionOperator inputs.
Allow freeze_orbitals to freeze specified occupied orbitals and specified unoccupied orbitals by removing operators on those modes from each term.
Preserve fermionic anticommutation signs when freezing orbitals changes the ordering parity of surviving operators.
Drop any term that vanishes because a frozen orbital occupation is incompatible with the ladder operators acting on that mode.
Renumber the surviving orbital indices so the returned FermionOperator has no unused index gaps.
Keep existing normal-ordering and molecular-term classification behavior unchanged.

interface.Name: freeze_orbitals
interface.Description: Returns a FermionOperator with the specified occupied and unoccupied orbitals frozen out.

problem_statement: OpenFermion needs a specialized Hamiltonian representation for electronic-structure models with a diagonal Coulomb term so that these operators can be stored more compactly and transformed more directly than a generic FermionOperator. Users need a DiagonalCoulombHamiltonian representation together with conversion routines back to FermionOperator form, support for Jordan-Wigner mapping, sparse-operator conversion, and the same qubit-count and validity checks expected by the surrounding transform utilities.
requirements: Provide a DiagonalCoulombHamiltonian representation for Hamiltonians with Hermitian one-body terms, real symmetric diagonal Coulomb terms, and an optional constant term.
Allow valid diagonal-Coulomb FermionOperator instances to be converted into DiagonalCoulombHamiltonian form and converted back without changing the represented Hamiltonian.

Reject non-FermionOperator inputs with TypeError, and raise ValueError for non-diagonal or unsupported FermionOperator terms, non-real diagonal-Coulomb coefficients, or too-small requested qubit counts.
Allow jordan_wigner to accept a DiagonalCoulombHamiltonian and produce the same QubitOperator as applying Jordan-Wigner to the equivalent FermionOperator for supported diagonal-Coulomb inputs.
Allow get_sparse_operator to accept a DiagonalCoulombHamiltonian and return the same sparse operator as the Jordan-Wigner image of the equivalent FermionOperator.
Keep the existing FermionOperator, InteractionOperator, QuadraticHamiltonian, and QubitOperator conversion behavior working.

interface.Name: DiagonalCoulombHamiltonian
interface.Description: Stores Hamiltonians with a Hermitian one-body matrix, a real symmetric diagonal Coulomb matrix, and a constant term.

interface.Name: get_diagonal_coulomb_hamiltonian
interface.Description: Converts a valid diagonal-Coulomb FermionOperator into DiagonalCoulombHamiltonian form, rejecting non-FermionOperator inputs with TypeError and invalid representation or qubit-count cases with ValueError.

interface.Name: get_fermion_operator
interface.Description: Converts supported structured operator representations into FermionOperator form.

interface.Name: jordan_wigner
interface.Description: Maps supported fermionic operator representations into the Jordan-Wigner qubit representation.

interface.Name: get_sparse_operator
interface.Description: Converts supported operators into sparse-matrix form, using the Jordan-Wigner image for non-QubitOperator inputs.

problem_statement: OpenFermion should support the conventional unnormalized Majorana operator convention and a more convenient way to construct those operators, so users can work with c_p and d_p style Majorana terms directly while keeping downstream quadratic-Hamiltonian and auxiliary-stabilizer workflows consistent with the updated definition.
requirements: Allow majorana_operator to construct Type 0 and Type 1 Majorana operators using the unnormalized convention a_p^ + a_p and i(a_p^ - a_p).
Allow majorana_operator to accept string shorthands such as c2 and d3 for Majorana operators on a given mode.
Allow majorana_operator() with no term to return the zero FermionOperator.
Reject nonscalar coefficients and invalid Majorana operator type specifications with ValueError.
Keep QuadraticHamiltonian.majorana_form output compatible with reconstruction using the updated majorana_operator convention.
Keep existing spin-operator helpers and Verstraete-Cirac locality behavior unchanged.

interface.Name: majorana_operator
interface.Description: Constructs a single Majorana operator term from tuple or string Majorana notation.

interface.Name: majorana_form
interface.Description: Returns the Majorana-form matrix and constant in a convention compatible with the library's Majorana operator helper.

problem_statement: OpenFermion needs a tree-based Bravyi-Kitaev transform so users can convert fermionic operators with the Bravyi-Kitaev tree formulation, especially when working with systems whose mode count is not a power of two, while preserving the existing Bravyi-Kitaev API expectations around identities, qubit-count validation, and spectral equivalence for simple observables.
requirements: Provide a bravyi_kitaev_tree transform for FermionOperator inputs.
Allow bravyi_kitaev_tree to map the identity operator to the identity QubitOperator.
Reject bravyi_kitaev_tree calls whose explicit n_qubits is smaller than the operator requires.
Produce tree-based Bravyi-Kitaev qubit operators whose number-operator spectra agree with the corresponding Jordan-Wigner results.
Keep the existing bravyi_kitaev transform behavior unchanged.

interface.Name: bravyi_kitaev_tree
interface.Description: Applies the tree-based Bravyi-Kitaev transform to a fermionic operator.

interface.Name: FenwickTree
interface.Description: Represents the Fenwick-tree data structure used by the tree-based Bravyi-Kitaev transform.

problem_statement: OpenFermion should provide an efficient Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff expansion helper so users can combine exponentials of noncommuting operators or matrices without hand-coding nested commutators, while still rejecting unsupported input combinations cleanly.
requirements: Provide a bch_expand helper that computes a truncated Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff expansion for two inputs of the same operator-like type.

Allow bch_expand to work with matrix-like inputs that support addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication, and produce results that agree with the baseline nested-commutator expansion through the requested order.
Reject inputs whose two operands do not have the same type.
Reject invalid truncation orders.

interface.Name: bch_expand
interface.Output: same type as x and y
interface.Description: Returns the truncated Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff expansion for two same-typed operator-like inputs.

problem_statement: OpenFermion operators need to support symbolic amplitudes so users can represent FermionOperator and related symbolic operators with unknown coefficients and still apply the standard fermion-to-qubit transforms. The implementation should allow sympy expressions to participate in the core symbolic-operator arithmetic used by FermionOperator construction and scalar multiplication, while preserving the expected Jordan-Wigner and Bravyi-Kitaev transformed coefficients.
requirements: Allow SymbolicOperator-derived operators to be constructed with sympy.Expr coefficients.
Allow SymbolicOperator scalar multiplication and in-place addition logic to work correctly when coefficients are sympy.Expr values, including cancellation of exact symbolic opposites.
Allow Jordan-Wigner transforms of FermionOperator inputs with symbolic coefficients to produce QubitOperator terms with the corresponding symbolic coefficients.
Allow Bravyi-Kitaev transforms of FermionOperator inputs with symbolic coefficients to produce the same transformed term structure and symbolic coefficients as the numeric case.

interface.Name: SymbolicOperator
interface.Description: Base class for symbolic quantum operators whose coefficients must now accept both numeric scalars and sympy expressions.

interface.Name: __mul__
interface.Description: Returns a new symbolic operator when multiplied by a supported scalar coefficient or another operator of the same type.

interface.Name: __rmul__
interface.Description: Supports left scalar multiplication of symbolic operators by supported scalar coefficient types.

interface.Name: __imul__
interface.Description: Performs in-place scalar or same-type operator multiplication while preserving symbolic coefficients.

interface.Name: __iadd__
interface.Description: Performs in-place addition and removes terms whose resulting symbolic coefficient simplifies to zero.

interface.Name: jordan_wigner
interface.Description: Maps FermionOperator inputs into the Jordan-Wigner qubit representation while preserving supported symbolic coefficients.

interface.Name: bravyi_kitaev
interface.Description: Maps FermionOperator inputs into the Bravyi-Kitaev qubit representation while preserving supported symbolic coefficients.

problem_statement: OpenFermion needs a native Majorana-operator representation so users can express fermionic models directly in the Majorana basis instead of encoding these products indirectly through other operator classes. The implementation should provide a MajoranaOperator type with the expected canonical term normalization, algebraic operations, string formatting, and public package export.
requirements: Provide a MajoranaOperator class that canonicalizes Majorana terms by sorting indices, removing repeated pairs, and applying the corresponding parity sign change.

Allow MajoranaOperator instances to test commutation, add, subtract, multiply, divide by scalars, and format themselves in a canonical Majorana representation, including empty products as `()` and the zero operator as `0`.
Allow scalar and operator multiplication to combine Majorana terms with the correct coefficient updates and merged-term parity.
Expose MajoranaOperator through the public openfermion package import path.

interface.Name: MajoranaOperator
interface.Description: Represents linear combinations of Majorana-operator products and normalizes single-term inputs into canonical order.

interface.Name: commutes_with
interface.Description: Tests commutation against another MajoranaOperator and rejects unsupported operand types.

interface.Name: __mul__
interface.Description: Supports multiplication by another MajoranaOperator or by numeric scalars using Majorana-term merge rules.

interface.Name: __truediv__
interface.Description: Supports division of a MajoranaOperator by numeric scalars.

interface.Name: __str__
interface.Description: Formats MajoranaOperator terms in the canonical human-readable representation: coefficients followed by parenthesized Majorana index tuples, with the identity or empty product rendered as `()` and the zero operator rendered as `0`.

problem_statement: OpenFermion's square-lattice Hubbard utilities need to distinguish horizontal and vertical nearest-neighbor edges so users can assign different tunneling and interaction coefficients along the two lattice directions instead of treating every nearest-neighbor bond as a single undifferentiated edge type.
requirements: Extend HubbardSquareLattice so square-lattice edge handling distinguishes onsite, generic neighbor, horizontal_neighbor, and vertical_neighbor edge types.
Allow HubbardSquareLattice to enumerate and count horizontal and vertical nearest-neighbor site pairs independently while preserving the existing generic neighbor behavior.
Allow FermiHubbardModel on a HubbardSquareLattice to accept tunneling and interaction parameter tuples keyed by horizontal_neighbor and vertical_neighbor edge types.
Generate Hamiltonian terms for direction-specific square-lattice neighbor parameters with the same multiplicity rules used for the corresponding onsite and generic-neighbor terms.

interface.Name: HubbardSquareLattice
interface.Input: constructor: x_dimension, y_dimension, n_dofs=1, spinless=False, periodic=True
interface.Description: Represents a square Hubbard lattice and exposes direction-aware nearest-neighbor edge categories.

interface.Name: edge_types
interface.Description: Returns the supported square-lattice edge-type labels, including horizontal_neighbor and vertical_neighbor.

interface.Name: validate_edge_type
interface.Description: Accepts the supported square-lattice edge-type labels and rejects unsupported ones.

interface.Name: site_pairs_iter
interface.Description: Enumerates onsite, generic neighbor, horizontal-neighbor, or vertical-neighbor site pairs for a square lattice.

interface.Name: n_horizontal_neighbor_pairs
interface.Description: Returns the number of horizontal nearest-neighbor site pairs on the square lattice.

interface.Name: n_vertical_neighbor_pairs
interface.Description: Returns the number of vertical nearest-neighbor site pairs on the square lattice.

interface.Name: FermiHubbardModel
interface.Description: Builds a lattice Hubbard model from edge-typed tunneling and interaction parameter tuples defined on the supplied lattice.

problem_statement: OpenFermion should support a more general tensor representation for fermionic operators so code can work with coefficient tensors for different creation and annihilation patterns, while still preserving existing interaction-operator iteration behavior and basis-rotation support.
requirements: Provide a PolynomialTensor representation for fermionic operator coefficients keyed by the creation and annihilation pattern of each tensor block.
Expose PolynomialTensor from openfermion.ops.
Allow PolynomialTensor basis rotations to work for spinful tensors by expanding an orbital rotation matrix across spin sectors when needed.
Reject addition, subtraction, and multiplication between PolynomialTensor instances when their tensor-key layouts do not match.
Keep existing InteractionOperator unique-iteration behavior unchanged.

interface.Name: PolynomialTensor
interface.Description: Represents fermionic coefficient tensors keyed by creation and annihilation pattern tuples.

interface.Name: __add__
interface.Description: Returns the sum of two PolynomialTensor instances and raises TypeError when their tensor-key layouts are incompatible.

interface.Name: __sub__
interface.Description: Returns the difference of two PolynomialTensor instances and raises TypeError when their tensor-key layouts are incompatible.

interface.Name: __mul__
interface.Description: Returns the elementwise product of two PolynomialTensor instances and raises TypeError when their tensor-key layouts are incompatible.

interface.Name: rotate_basis
interface.Description: Rotates every stored tensor block into a new basis and expands orbital rotations across spin sectors for spinful tensors.

problem_statement: OpenFermion needs a Majorana-operator conversion path for fermionic Hamiltonians so users can move between FermionOperator-based models and the Majorana representation without manually expanding each ladder operator term. The implementation should provide the Majorana conversion routine for fermionic operators, accept diagonal Coulomb Hamiltonians through the same path, and preserve the expected type checking for unsupported inputs.
requirements: Provide a Majorana conversion routine for FermionOperator instances using the standard mapping from fermionic creation and annihilation operators to Majorana modes.
Allow converting a DiagonalCoulombHamiltonian to a MajoranaOperator through the same public conversion entry point used for FermionOperator inputs.
Ensure converting a DiagonalCoulombHamiltonian yields the same MajoranaOperator as converting the equivalent FermionOperator.
Raise TypeError when the Majorana conversion entry point or its validated helper entry points receive unsupported input types.
Keep the existing diagonal-Coulomb conversion path and Majorana-to-Fermion conversion behavior working.

interface.Name: get_majorana_operator
interface.Description: Converts supported fermionic operator representations into their equivalent MajoranaOperator form.

interface.Name: _fermion_operator_to_majorana_operator
interface.Description: Converts a FermionOperator into a MajoranaOperator and rejects unsupported input types.

interface.Name: _fermion_term_to_majorana_operator
interface.Description: Converts a single FermionOperator term into its MajoranaOperator representation and rejects unsupported input types.

interface.Name: get_diagonal_coulomb_hamiltonian
interface.Description: Converts a supported FermionOperator into DiagonalCoulombHamiltonian form for downstream structured conversions.

interface.Name: get_fermion_operator
interface.Description: Converts supported structured operators into FermionOperator form, including the existing MajoranaOperator conversion path.

problem_statement: OpenFermion can apply the Bravyi-Kitaev transform to FermionOperator and MajoranaOperator inputs, but chemistry workflows that already use InteractionOperator still have to convert through a FermionOperator first. Users need Bravyi-Kitaev support to work directly on InteractionOperator instances, including the same validation around qubit counts and the same transformed qubit operator semantics as the existing FermionOperator path.
requirements: Allow bravyi_kitaev to accept an InteractionOperator directly.

When given an InteractionOperator, produce the same QubitOperator as applying bravyi_kitaev to the equivalent FermionOperator for one-body, Coulomb/exchange, number-excitation, double-excitation, and complex-valued interaction terms.
Preserve the existing n_qubits validation behavior for InteractionOperator inputs and raise ValueError when the requested qubit count is too small.
Keep the existing Bravyi-Kitaev behavior for FermionOperator and MajoranaOperator inputs working.

interface.Name: bravyi_kitaev
interface.Description: Transforms supported fermionic operator representations into the Bravyi-Kitaev qubit representation while preserving the existing qubit-count validation rules.

problem_statement: PennyLane has QML templates and PyTorch support, but users do not have a native way to wrap a QNode as a PyTorch neural-network layer. A QNode should be usable inside standard torch.nn modules and hybrid models while keeping its quantum weights trainable through PyTorch.
requirements: A Torch-compatible QNode layer must be available from the qnn module.
The layer must be constructible from a QNode and a mapping of QNode weight names to shapes.
The layer must behave as a torch.nn.Module and evaluate the wrapped QNode for single inputs and batched inputs.
Trainable QNode weights must be registered as PyTorch parameters with gradients populated by backpropagation.
The layer must be usable inside a larger torch.nn.Module together with classical layers.

interface.Name: TorchLayer
interface.Description: Wraps a PennyLane QNode as a PyTorch module with trainable QNode weights.

interface.Name: TorchLayer.forward
interface.Description: Evaluates the wrapped QNode for single or batched PyTorch inputs.

problem_statement: The kernels utility functions for building square and rectangular kernel matrices are tied to NumPy-style array construction. They should work with PennyLane's supported autodiff interfaces and with kernel functions that return batched values, such as shot-vector outputs, while preserving the existing scalar kernel matrix behavior.
requirements: Square and rectangular kernel matrix helpers must preserve scalar kernel outputs and return matrices with the expected training and test data dimensions.
Kernel matrix helpers must support differentiable Autograd inputs without breaking gradient computation through the input data.
Kernel functions that return one-dimensional batched values must produce a stack of kernel matrices with the batch dimension leading.
Assuming a normalized square kernel must fill the diagonal with values that match the interface and shape of the kernel output.

interface.Name: square_kernel_matrix
interface.Description: Computes the symmetric kernel matrix for one dataset, supporting autodiff-compatible arrays and scalar or batched kernel outputs.

interface.Name: kernel_matrix
interface.Description: Computes the rectangular kernel matrix between two datasets, supporting autodiff-compatible arrays and scalar or batched kernel outputs.

problem_statement: The qchem tapering workflow can require excessive peak memory when tapering Hamiltonians with many Pauli terms because the Clifford-transformed PauliSentence is multiplied through the whole Hamiltonian at once. The tapering implementation should keep the same physical result while reducing peak memory by processing the Hamiltonian in smaller PauliSentence chunks.
requirements: Tapering a Hamiltonian must continue to return the same tapered Hamiltonian as the PauliSentence-based tapering path.
The PauliSentence tapering path must be able to process large PauliSentence inputs in bounded-size chunks rather than materializing the full transformed expression at once.
Splitting a PauliSentence into chunks must preserve every original PauliWord and coefficient exactly when the chunks are recombined.
The public qchem tapering workflow must preserve expectation values for representative tapered observables and Hartree-Fock states.

interface.Name: taper
interface.Description: Transforms and tapers a Hamiltonian while using the memory-bounded PauliSentence tapering path.

interface.Name: _taper_pauli_sentence
interface.Description: Internal PauliSentence tapering helper used by the public taper workflow.

interface.Name: _split_pauli_sentence
interface.Description: Splits a PauliSentence into smaller chunks without dropping terms.

problem_statement: PennyLane supports converting fermionic operators to qubit operators, but users also need a parity-basis mapping in addition to the existing Jordan-Wigner path. The fermionic conversion utilities should expose a parity transform that maps FermiWord and FermiSentence objects to equivalent qubit operators or Pauli sentences, with support for explicit wire labels and coefficient tolerance handling.
requirements: A public parity transform must be available for fermionic operators.
The transform must accept FermiWord and FermiSentence inputs and reject incompatible operator types with a clear ValueError.
The caller must provide the number of qubits or spin orbitals, and the transform must reject fermionic terms that address orbitals outside that system size.
The transform must be able to return either a PennyLane qubit operator or a PauliSentence, depending on the requested output mode.
Identity and empty fermionic operators must produce valid identity or zero qubit representations.
The transform must support custom wire mappings for both word and sentence inputs.
Small imaginary coefficient components must be removable according to the requested tolerance.
Using the parity mapping must emit the documented warning that operators and states should be in the parity basis.

interface.Name: parity_transform
interface.Description: Converts FermiWord and FermiSentence objects into qubit representations using the parity mapping.

problem_statement: PennyLane can represent qubit observables and fermionic operators, while quantum chemistry users often need to exchange those objects with OpenFermion. The repository should provide a direct conversion path between PennyLane operator or fermionic representations and OpenFermion's qubit and fermion operator representations, including support for wire mappings and small imaginary numerical noise.
requirements: PennyLane qubit operators made from sums, products, and linear combinations of Pauli words must be convertible to equivalent OpenFermion QubitOperator objects.
PennyLane FermiWord and FermiSentence objects must be convertible to equivalent OpenFermion FermionOperator objects.

OpenFermion QubitOperator objects must be convertible back into PennyLane qubit-operator containers with matching coefficients and wires, using the requested supported PennyLane output style when the lower-level qubit helper is called directly.
OpenFermion FermionOperator objects must be convertible back into PennyLane fermionic representations.
Explicit wire mappings must be honored in both conversion directions for qubit wires and fermionic orbital labels, and mappings that do not cover all required labels must be rejected.
The conversion routines must drop imaginary coefficient parts only when they are below the requested tolerance and must preserve them when they exceed that tolerance.

Unsupported top-level input objects, unsupported qubit output-style selectors, or non-Pauli PennyLane operators nested inside compound qubit expressions must raise clear ValueError exceptions instead of producing invalid or partial conversions.

interface.Name: from_openfermion
interface.Output: PennyLane LinearCombination, Sum, FermiWord, or FermiSentence
interface.Description: Converts OpenFermion qubit and fermion operators into PennyLane representations while preserving coefficients, labels, and requested wire mappings.

interface.Name: _from_openfermion_qubit
interface.Output: PennyLane LinearCombination or Sum, according to the requested supported format
interface.Description: Internal conversion helper for OpenFermion QubitOperator conversion. It should support the repository's qubit-container output styles and reject unsupported format selectors with ValueError.

interface.Name: to_openfermion
interface.Input: PennyLane Sum, LinearCombination, FermiWord, or FermiSentence; wires=None; tol=1e-16
interface.Description: Converts PennyLane qubit and fermionic representations into OpenFermion operators. Wire mappings apply to qubit wires and fermionic orbital labels, and non-Pauli qubit components must be rejected before producing a partial OpenFermion operator.

interface.Name: FermiWord.to_string
interface.Description: Returns the OpenFermion-compatible string form needed for fermionic conversion, applying wire_map to fermionic orbital labels when provided.

problem_statement: PennyLane has fermionic data structures that can be manipulated symbolically, but users also need to obtain their concrete matrix representations for downstream simulation and verification workflows. Fermionic words and fermionic sentences should support converting themselves into matrices using the standard fermion-to-qubit mapping while respecting the number of orbitals requested by the caller.
requirements: FermiWord objects must provide a matrix representation of the fermionic operator they encode.
FermiSentence objects must provide a matrix representation equal to the weighted sum of the matrices of their fermionic terms.
When the number of orbitals is not provided, the matrix dimension must be inferred from the largest orbital index present in the object.
When the caller provides a number of orbitals, the returned matrix must use that orbital count.
If the requested number of orbitals is smaller than the number required by the fermionic object, a clear ValueError must be raised.

interface.Name: FermiWord.to_mat
interface.Description: Returns the matrix representation of a fermionic word, inferring or validating the orbital count.

interface.Name: FermiSentence.to_mat
interface.Description: Returns the matrix representation of a fermionic sentence as a weighted operator sum, inferring or validating the orbital count.

problem_statement: PennyLane's TorchLayer only supports either a single input vector or a simple batch of input vectors. It should behave like common neural-network layers and accept inputs with extra leading dimensions, applying the wrapped quantum node across those dimensions while preserving the expected output shape and gradient flow.
requirements: TorchLayer must accept one-dimensional inputs and ordinary batched two-dimensional inputs with the existing output shapes.
TorchLayer must accept inputs with multiple leading dimensions before the per-example quantum input dimension.
For multidimensional inputs, TorchLayer must evaluate the wrapped quantum node across the leading dimensions and return outputs with those leading dimensions followed by the quantum output dimension.
Backpropagation through multidimensional TorchLayer inputs must still populate gradients for all trainable QNode weights.

interface.Name: TorchLayer
interface.Description: Wraps a PennyLane QNode as a PyTorch module with trainable QNode weights.

interface.Name: TorchLayer.forward
interface.Description: Evaluates the wrapped QNode for single, batched, or multidimensional inputs while preserving leading dimensions.

problem_statement: PortfolioOptimization currently models each asset decision as binary, so a portfolio can only choose whether to buy an asset or not. This prevents users from representing integer asset holdings, where the portfolio should be able to buy multiple units of the same asset within configured bounds. The finance optimization workflow needs PortfolioOptimization to support integer decision variables while preserving the existing binary behavior when no bounds are provided.
requirements: PortfolioOptimization must continue to create binary decision variables when no bounds are provided.
PortfolioOptimization must accept optional per-asset integer bounds and use them to create integer decision variables in the quadratic program.
The generated quadratic program must preserve the existing portfolio objective and budget constraint behavior for both binary and bounded-integer configurations.
PortfolioOptimization must reject incompatible expected-return, covariance, and bounds shapes with QiskitFinanceError.
PortfolioOptimization must reject bounds whose upper bound is smaller than the lower bound.
PortfolioOptimization must expose readable and writable bounds configuration for the portfolio model.

interface.Name: PortfolioOptimization
interface.Input: constructor: expected_returns, covariances, risk_factor, budget, bounds=None
interface.Description: Portfolio optimization application supports either binary asset decisions or bounded integer asset holdings.

interface.Name: PortfolioOptimization.to_quadratic_program
interface.Description: Builds a quadratic program whose variables are binary when bounds is unset and integer-bounded when bounds is configured.

interface.Name: PortfolioOptimization.bounds
interface.Description: Property getter and setter expose the optional lower and upper integer bounds for each asset variable.

problem_statement: The probability distribution circuits in qiskit-finance currently expose their implementation gates directly at the top level. This makes the library circuits draw as decomposed gate sequences instead of compact named blocks, which is inconsistent with the wrapped circuit-library behavior used elsewhere in Qiskit. The probability distribution circuits should be wrapped so they remain compact at the outer level while preserving the same decomposed behavior and validation semantics they already provide.
requirements: UniformDistribution must construct a wrapped top-level circuit instead of exposing the raw Hadamard layer at the outermost level.
NormalDistribution and LogNormalDistribution must preserve their existing decomposed state-preparation behavior after being wrapped.
Calling decompose() on the wrapped probability distribution circuits must recover the same underlying circuit semantics as before the wrapping change.
NormalDistribution must continue to reject invalid bounds and mismatching dimension shapes with the same error behavior as before.
LogNormalDistribution must continue to preserve the existing discretized probability-distribution behavior for the covered univariate and multivariate configurations.

interface.Name: UniformDistribution
interface.Description: Constructs a wrapped uniform probability distribution circuit whose decomposed form is the expected Hadamard layer.

interface.Name: NormalDistribution
interface.Input: constructor: num_qubits, mu=None, sigma=None, bounds=None, upto_diag=False, name="P(X)"
interface.Description: Constructs a wrapped normal probability distribution circuit without changing the decomposed distribution semantics or validation behavior.

interface.Name: LogNormalDistribution
interface.Input: constructor: num_qubits, mu=None, sigma=None, bounds=None, upto_diag=False, name="P(X)"
interface.Description: Constructs a wrapped log-normal probability distribution circuit while preserving the decomposed distribution semantics covered by the tests.

problem_statement: Neural-network model training does not currently give users a supported way to observe intermediate optimization progress. Users need trainable neural-network classifier workflows to accept a callback during construction and invoke it while fitting so loss-related values and optimizer weights can be tracked during training.
requirements: Neural-network classifiers must accept an optional callback when they are constructed.
When a callback is supplied, classifier fitting must invoke it during optimization with the current objective weights and computed objective value.
Callback objective values must be provided as floats.
Callback weight values must match the neural network's trainable weight dimension and be provided as numeric values.
Classifier training and scoring must continue to work for circuit-based and two-layer neural network classifiers across existing optimizer, loss, and simulator configurations.
Classifier behavior must remain unchanged when no callback is supplied.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkClassifier
interface.Input: constructor: neural_network, loss='squared_error', one_hot=False, optimizer=None, warm_start=False, initial_point=None, callback=None
interface.Description: Classifier constructor accepts an optional callback used to observe objective weights and objective values during training.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkClassifier.fit
interface.Description: Fits the classifier and invokes the configured callback during objective evaluation when a callback is present.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkClassifier.score
interface.Description: Scores fitted classifier workflows after training with or without a callback.

interface.Name: TrainableModel
interface.Input: constructor: neural_network, loss='squared_error', optimizer=None, warm_start=False, initial_point=None, callback=None
interface.Description: Base trainable model stores the optional callback used by classifier training.

interface.Name: TrainableModel._get_objective
interface.Description: Returns an objective callable that evaluates the objective and invokes the configured callback with weights and value.

problem_statement: Neural-network classifiers and regressors should let users provide an initial point for model training. Today the only way to control the starting weights is to rely on warm-start behavior and private fit state, which is awkward for users who want a clean public way to start optimization from known weights.
requirements: Trainable neural-network models accept an optional initial point for optimizer weights.
The initial point is exposed as a readable and writable model property.
When an initial point is provided, training passes it to the optimizer instead of choosing a random starting point.
If warm start is enabled and the model already has a previous fit result, the previous fitted weights take precedence as the next initial point.
When neither warm-start weights nor a user-provided initial point is available, training still chooses a random point with the correct number of neural-network weights.
The initial-point option is available through the neural-network classifier and regressor APIs, including VQC and VQR wrappers.

interface.Name: TrainableModel
interface.Input: constructor: neural_network, loss, optimizer, warm_start, initial_point
interface.Description: Base trainable model that stores an optional optimizer initial point.

interface.Name: TrainableModel.initial_point
interface.Description: Property exposing the current optimizer initial point and allowing it to be reassigned.

interface.Name: TrainableModel._choose_initial_point
interface.Description: Chooses optimizer starting weights from warm-start fit results, the stored initial point, or a random vector.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkClassifier
interface.Input: constructor: neural_network, loss, one_hot, optimizer, warm_start, initial_point
interface.Description: Classifier wrapper that accepts and uses an optimizer initial point during fit.

interface.Name: VQC
interface.Input: constructor: num_qubits, feature_map, ansatz, loss, optimizer, warm_start, quantum_instance, initial_point
interface.Description: Variational quantum classifier wrapper that forwards the initial point to its trainable classifier base.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkRegressor
interface.Input: constructor: neural_network, loss, optimizer, warm_start, initial_point
interface.Description: Regressor wrapper that accepts and uses an optimizer initial point during fit.

interface.Name: VQR
interface.Input: constructor: num_qubits, feature_map, ansatz, loss, optimizer, warm_start, quantum_instance, initial_point
interface.Description: Variational quantum regressor wrapper that forwards the initial point to its trainable regressor base.

problem_statement: QuantumKernel should support feature maps that contain user-tunable parameters in addition to data-encoding parameters. Users need to mark which feature-map parameters are trainable, assign or reassign them independently of input data, inspect whether any remain unbound, and keep the original unbound feature map available while the working feature map is updated.
requirements: QuantumKernel can be constructed with a feature map and an explicit collection of user-tunable parameters.
The kernel tracks user parameters separately from data parameters and exposes the current user-parameter bindings.
Assigning user-parameter values accepts both ordered values and parameter-to-value mappings.
Assigning the wrong number of ordered values or unknown parameters raises ValueError.
Repeated assignments update existing bindings without losing previous bound values.
The original unbound feature map remains available after user parameters have been bound.

interface.Name: QuantumKernel
interface.Input: constructor: feature_map, enforce_psd, batch_size, quantum_instance, user_parameters
interface.Description: Kernel class that can track tunable feature-map parameters separately from data-encoding parameters.

interface.Name: QuantumKernel.assign_user_parameters
interface.Description: Assigns user-tunable feature-map parameters from an ordered sequence or parameter mapping and raises ValueError for incompatible assignments.

interface.Name: QuantumKernel.bind_user_parameters
interface.Description: Alternate binding entry point for assigning user-tunable parameter values.

interface.Name: QuantumKernel.get_unbound_parameters
interface.Description: Returns user parameters that are still not bound to numeric values.

interface.Name: QuantumKernel.user_parameters
interface.Description: Property exposing the user-tunable parameters tracked by the kernel.

interface.Name: QuantumKernel.user_param_binds
interface.Description: Property exposing the current mapping from tracked user parameters to bound values or replacement parameters.

interface.Name: QuantumKernel.unbound_feature_map
interface.Description: Property returning the original feature map before user-parameter values are bound.

problem_statement: Qiskit Machine Learning provides quantum kernels that can be evaluated and used in kernel-based classifiers, but there is no built-in training component for tuning parameterized quantum kernels against labeled data. Users need a trainer that optimizes the trainable parameters of a QuantumKernel with a kernel-specific loss and returns an optimized kernel that can be used by downstream classifiers.
requirements: Provide a QuantumKernelTrainer that accepts a QuantumKernel with trainable user parameters, an optional kernel loss, an optional optimizer, and an optional initial point.
QuantumKernelTrainer.fit must optimize the kernel user parameters against labeled training data and return a result object containing optimizer metadata and an optimized QuantumKernel.
The input QuantumKernel must not be mutated by training; the fitted result must carry the optimized kernel state.
Provide a KernelLoss abstraction and an SVCLoss implementation usable by the trainer, including support for passing SVC keyword arguments.
Training must reject quantum kernels that do not expose trainable user parameters.

interface.Name: QuantumKernelTrainer
interface.Description: Creates a trainer for optimizing the user parameters of a QuantumKernel with a kernel loss and optimizer.

interface.Name: QuantumKernelTrainer.fit
interface.Description: Fits the trainer on labeled data and returns optimization results with an optimized quantum kernel.

interface.Name: QuantumKernelTrainerResult
interface.Description: Stores optimizer results and exposes the optimized QuantumKernel through quantum_kernel.

interface.Name: KernelLoss
interface.Description: Defines the callable and evaluate contract for kernel loss functions used by QuantumKernelTrainer.

interface.Name: SVCLoss
interface.Description: Computes a support-vector-classifier-based loss for a parameterized QuantumKernel and forwards keyword arguments to sklearn.svm.SVC.

interface.Name: SVCLoss.evaluate
interface.Description: Assigns user parameters, evaluates the kernel matrix, fits an SVC, and returns the kernel training loss.

problem_statement: VQC currently requires users to provide one-hot encoded labels, which makes ordinary classification workflows inconvenient when labels are already represented as integers or categorical strings. Users should be able to train, score, and predict with VQC using plain class labels while preserving the original label representation in predictions.
requirements: VQC must accept one-dimensional integer class labels without requiring callers to one-hot encode them first.
VQC must accept categorical string labels and train them through the same classifier workflow.
Predictions from VQC and NeuralNetworkClassifier must be decoded back to the original label representation when labels were encoded during fitting.
Existing one-hot label validation and class-count behavior must continue to work for classifier workflows.

interface.Name: VQC
interface.Input: constructor: num_qubits, feature_map, ansatz, loss, optimizer, quantum_instance, initial_point, callback
interface.Description: Creates a variational quantum classifier that accepts one-hot labels, integer class labels, or categorical string labels for training.

interface.Name: VQC.fit
interface.Description: Fits the classifier after validating and internally encoding integer or categorical labels as needed.

interface.Name: VQC.predict
interface.Description: Returns predicted labels using the original label representation learned during fitting.

interface.Name: VQC.score
interface.Description: Scores predictions against labels supplied in the same plain, categorical, or one-hot representation accepted by fitting.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkClassifier
interface.Input: constructor: neural_network, loss, one_hot, optimizer, warm_start, initial_point, callback
interface.Description: Provides classifier label validation, encoding, fitting, prediction, and scoring for quantum neural network classifiers.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkClassifier.predict
interface.Description: Returns predictions decoded to categorical labels when the classifier was fit with categorical targets.

problem_statement: Qiskit Machine Learning users can train classifier and regressor models, but there is no native way to persist those trained models and restore them later. Users have to rely on ad hoc serialization or private internal state, which is unreliable for models that contain quantum-network or kernel objects. The model APIs should provide built-in save and load support so a trained model can be stored and then loaded for inference with the same behavior.
requirements: Trainable neural-network classifiers and regressors must be saveable to a user-provided file path and loadable from that file.
Kernel-based classifiers and regressors, including QSVC, QSVR, and PegasosQSVC, must be saveable to a user-provided file path and loadable from that file.
A loaded model must preserve fitted model state well enough that predictions on the same input match the predictions from the model before it was saved.
Loading through a model class must verify that the serialized object is an instance of that class.
Loading a serialized model through an incompatible model class must raise TypeError.

interface.Name: SerializableModelMixin
interface.Description: Mixin for machine-learning models that provides save and load methods using dill serialization.

interface.Name: SerializableModelMixin.save
interface.Description: Serializes the model instance to the specified file path.

interface.Name: SerializableModelMixin.load
interface.Description: Loads a model from the specified file path and raises TypeError if the loaded object is not an instance of the class used to load it.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkClassifier
interface.Input: constructor: neural_network, loss='squared_error', one_hot: bool = False, optimizer=None, warm_start: bool = False, initial_point=None, callback=None
interface.Description: Trainable classifier that supports saving and loading fitted model state.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkRegressor
interface.Input: constructor: neural_network, loss='squared_error', optimizer=None, warm_start: bool = False, initial_point=None, callback=None
interface.Description: Trainable regressor that supports saving and loading fitted model state.

interface.Name: QSVC
interface.Description: Quantum support vector classifier that supports saving and loading fitted model state.

interface.Name: QSVR
interface.Description: Quantum support vector regressor that supports saving and loading fitted model state.

interface.Name: PegasosQSVC
interface.Input: constructor: quantum_kernel=None, C=1.0, num_steps=1000, precomputed=False, seed=None
interface.Description: Pegasos quantum support vector classifier that supports saving and loading fitted model state.

problem_statement: QNN-based classifiers can train on dense labels, including one-hot encoded labels, but they fail when users provide sparse arrays such as the output of common one-hot encoders. This prevents workflows that naturally produce sparse feature or label matrices from being used directly with classifiers like VQC. Classifiers should accept sparse input arrays in the same user-facing training and scoring workflows that already work for dense arrays.
requirements: QNN-based classifiers must accept sparse feature arrays during fitting.
QNN-based classifiers must accept sparse label arrays during fitting.
QNN-based classifiers must accept sparse feature and label arrays during scoring.
Sparse arrays must be converted to dense arrays before they reach objective and loss computations that use NumPy operations.
Sparse one-hot labels must work with squared-error, absolute-error, and cross-entropy losses.
The sparse-array behavior must be available through both the generic neural-network classifier and VQC.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkClassifier
interface.Input: constructor: neural_network, loss='squared_error', one_hot: bool = False, optimizer=None, warm_start: bool = False, initial_point=None, callback=None
interface.Description: QNN-based classifier whose fit and score workflows accept sparse feature and label arrays by converting them to dense arrays for downstream numerical computations.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkClassifier.fit
interface.Description: Fits the classifier from dense or sparse feature and label arrays.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkClassifier.score
interface.Description: Scores the classifier using dense or sparse feature and label arrays.

interface.Name: VQC
interface.Input: constructor: num_qubits=None, feature_map=None, ansatz=None, loss='cross_entropy', optimizer=None, quantum_instance=None, callback=None
interface.Description: Variational quantum classifier that inherits sparse feature and sparse label handling from the neural-network classifier workflow.

problem_statement: The neural-network module does not provide a built-in way to estimate the effective dimension of quantum neural networks. Users who want to compare model capacity globally or around a fixed parameter point must implement the effective-dimension workflow themselves. The repository should provide reusable effective-dimension utilities that work with the existing neural-network abstractions.
requirements: The implementation must provide global and local effective-dimension estimators for existing neural networks.
The estimators must accept either sample counts or explicit input and weight sample arrays, and validate that explicit arrays match the neural network's input and weight dimensions.
The global estimator must compute effective dimensions for a single dataset size or for an array of dataset sizes.
The local estimator must restrict weight samples to a single parameter point and reject multiple local weight points.
The estimators must support callback reporting while evaluating sampled gradients.

interface.Name: EffectiveDimension
interface.Description: Global effective-dimension estimator for a neural network, using generated or explicit input and weight samples.

interface.Name: LocalEffectiveDimension
interface.Description: Local effective-dimension estimator that accepts exactly one weight sample point.

interface.Name: EffectiveDimension.get_effective_dimension
interface.Description: Computes effective dimension for one dataset size or for multiple dataset sizes.

problem_statement: Training components in Qiskit Machine Learning currently expect optimizer objects with a minimize method. Users need the model and quantum-kernel training APIs to accept callable minimizers as optimizers too, so they can pass SciPy-style minimization functions or compatible custom callables without wrapping them in a Qiskit Optimizer class.
requirements: Trainable model APIs must accept either a Qiskit optimizer object, a callable minimizer, or no optimizer.
Callable optimizers must be invoked with the objective function, the selected initial point, and the objective gradient when fitting classifiers and regressors.
The default optimizer behavior must remain unchanged when no optimizer is supplied.
Neural-network classifiers must train, score, serialize, and continue supporting callbacks and warm starts when using callable optimizers.
Neural-network regressors must train, score, serialize, and continue supporting callbacks and warm starts when using callable optimizers.
QuantumKernelTrainer must accept callable optimizers and pass the objective function, initial point, gradient, and bounds expected by the callable minimizer.
Quantum-kernel training results must still bind trained kernel parameters and produce usable kernels after fitting.
Existing optimizer-object behavior for related classifier, regressor, VQC, VQR, QSVC, and QSVR workflows must remain compatible.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkClassifier
interface.Input: constructor: neural_network, loss="squared_error", one_hot=False, optimizer=None, warm_start=False, initial_point=None, callback=None
interface.Description: Classifier accepting either Qiskit optimizer objects or callable minimizers through the optimizer argument while preserving fit, score, callback, warm-start, and serialization behavior.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkClassifier.fit
interface.Description: Fits the classifier and invokes callable optimizers with the objective, initial point, and gradient.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkClassifier.score
interface.Description: Scores a classifier fitted with either an optimizer object or callable optimizer.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkRegressor
interface.Input: constructor: neural_network, loss="squared_error", optimizer=None, warm_start=False, initial_point=None, callback=None
interface.Description: Regressor accepting either Qiskit optimizer objects or callable minimizers through the optimizer argument while preserving fit, score, callback, warm-start, and serialization behavior.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkRegressor.fit
interface.Description: Fits the regressor and invokes callable optimizers with the objective, initial point, and gradient.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkRegressor.score
interface.Description: Scores a regressor fitted with either an optimizer object or callable optimizer.

interface.Name: QuantumKernelTrainer
interface.Description: Quantum-kernel trainer accepting either Qiskit optimizer objects or callable minimizers through the optimizer argument.

interface.Name: QuantumKernelTrainer.fit
interface.Description: Trains kernel parameters and invokes callable optimizers with objective, initial point, gradient, and bounds.

problem_statement: Trainable quantum machine-learning models can already be fit and then used for prediction, but users who want to inspect the learned parameters must read private fit state directly. This breaks the public model contract and makes trained model introspection depend on implementation details. Fitted trainable models should expose their trained weights and optimization result through public model APIs.
requirements: A fitted trainable model must provide public access to the trained weights.
A fitted trainable model must provide public access to the optimizer result produced during fitting.
The public trained-weight value must be a NumPy array matching the optimizer result's parameter vector.
The public trained-weight length must match the number of trainable parameters in the underlying neural network.
Classifiers and regressors derived from the trainable-model base must expose the same trained-weight and optimizer-result access after fitting.
Accessing the trained weights or optimizer result before the model has been fitted must raise the library's machine-learning error.

interface.Name: TrainableModel
interface.Input: constructor: neural_network, loss='squared_error', optimizer=None, warm_start: bool = False, initial_point=None, callback=None
interface.Description: Base trainable model whose fitted instances expose public fit_result and weights accessors matching the optimizer result, and whose unfitted instances raise QiskitMachineLearningError for those accessors.

interface.Name: TrainableModel.fit
interface.Description: Fits the trainable model and populates the optimizer result used by fit_result and weights.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkClassifier
interface.Input: constructor: neural_network, loss='squared_error', one_hot: bool = False, optimizer=None, warm_start: bool = False, initial_point=None, callback=None
interface.Description: Trainable classifier that inherits public fit_result and weights access behavior after fitting.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkRegressor
interface.Input: constructor: neural_network, loss='squared_error', optimizer=None, warm_start: bool = False, initial_point=None, callback=None
interface.Description: Trainable regressor that inherits public fit_result and weights access behavior after fitting.

problem_statement: PegasosQSVC can be trained and used for prediction, but calling its decision function follows the inherited scikit-learn SVC implementation and fails because PegasosQSVC does not maintain the internal SVC state expected by that parent method. Users should be able to inspect PegasosQSVC decision scores directly after fitting without hitting unrelated scikit-learn internals.
requirements: PegasosQSVC must expose a working decision-function method after fitting.
The decision function must return one score per input sample and must use the Pegasos quantum-kernel model's learned weighted kernel sum.
The sign of each returned decision score must agree with the class prediction boundary used by PegasosQSVC.
The predict method must continue to return the fitted classifier labels by applying the decision scores.
Calling the decision function before fitting must raise the library's machine-learning error.
Existing PegasosQSVC behavior for callable quantum kernels, precomputed kernels, changing kernels, and scoring must remain stable.

interface.Name: PegasosQSVC
interface.Input: constructor: quantum_kernel=None, C=1.0, num_steps=1000, precomputed=False, seed=None
interface.Description: Pegasos quantum support vector classifier that fits quantum-kernel training data and exposes prediction and decision-score behavior without depending on scikit-learn SVC internals.

interface.Name: PegasosQSVC.fit
interface.Description: Fits the Pegasos classifier on feature vectors or a precomputed kernel matrix.

interface.Name: PegasosQSVC.predict
interface.Description: Predicts labels by thresholding Pegasos decision scores.

interface.Name: PegasosQSVC.decision_function
interface.Description: Returns the fitted Pegasos weighted-kernel decision score for each input sample and validates fitted state and input shape.

problem_statement: The repository already provides quantum neural network abstractions, but users do not yet have a neural network implementation built directly on Qiskit's Sampler primitive. Users should be able to construct a sampling neural network from a parameterized circuit, evaluate probability-like outputs, compute gradients for training, and use this sampler-backed network through the variational quantum classifier workflow.
requirements: Provide a sampler-backed quantum neural network that is available from the neural network package.

The sampler-backed neural network must accept a parameterized quantum circuit, optional sampler primitive, input parameters, weight parameters, optional sparsity setting, optional interpretation function, optional output shape, optional gradient object, and an input-gradient setting.
When no sampler is supplied, the neural network must use a default Sampler primitive.
The neural network must support dense and sparse outputs.
The neural network must support raw bitstring-probability outputs as well as interpreted one-dimensional and multi-dimensional outputs.
Forward evaluation must return outputs with shapes determined by batch size and output shape.
Backward evaluation must return weight gradients and must return input gradients only when input-gradient computation is enabled.
The neural network must support circuits with only input parameters, only weight parameters, or both kinds of parameters.
SamplerQNN results and gradients must agree with the existing CircuitQNN behavior for equivalent circuits and interpret functions.
The variational quantum classifier must support a sampler-backed construction path while preserving the existing quantum-instance-based workflow.

interface.Name: SamplerQNN
interface.Input: constructor: circuit, sampler=None, input_params=None, weight_params=None, sparse: bool = False, interpret=None, output_shape=None, gradient=None, input_gradients: bool = False
interface.Description: Sampler-primitive neural network for sampling-probability outputs from parameterized circuits, exposing sparse, output_shape, input_params, weight_params, num_inputs, num_weights, and input_gradients behavior.

interface.Name: SamplerQNN.forward
interface.Description: Evaluates sampler outputs for input data and weights.

interface.Name: SamplerQNN.backward
interface.Description: Evaluates sampler-gradient backward results for input data and weights.

interface.Name: VQC
interface.Input: constructor: num_qubits=None, feature_map=None, ansatz=None, loss='cross_entropy', optimizer=None, warm_start: bool = False, quantum_instance=None, initial_point=None, callback=None, sampler=None
interface.Description: Variational quantum classifier that can use either the existing quantum-instance path or a sampler-backed neural network and exposes feature_map, ansatz, num_qubits, and num_classes behavior.

interface.Name: VQC.fit
interface.Description: Fits the variational classifier on classification data using the configured neural network and optimizer.

interface.Name: VQC.score
interface.Description: Scores the fitted variational classifier on classification data.

interface.Name: VQC.predict
interface.Description: Predicts labels for classification data.

interface.Name: VQC._get_interpret
interface.Description: Returns the parity-style interpretation callable used to map sampler outputs to class indices.

problem_statement: The repository already provides quantum neural network abstractions and regressor algorithms, but users do not yet have a neural network implementation built directly on Qiskit's Estimator primitive. Users should be able to construct a neural network from a parameterized circuit and observables, evaluate expectation-value outputs, compute gradients for training, and use this estimator-backed network through the existing variational quantum regressor workflow.
requirements: Provide an estimator-backed quantum neural network that is available from the neural network package.

The estimator-backed neural network must accept a parameterized quantum circuit, optional estimator primitive, optional observables, input parameters, weight parameters, optional gradient object, and an input-gradient setting.
When no estimator is supplied, the neural network must use a default Estimator primitive.
When no observables are supplied, the neural network must use a default Z observable over all circuit qubits.
The neural network must support one or more observables and return outputs with the corresponding output dimension.
Forward evaluation must handle scalar, vector, batched, and nested input data shapes consistently with the existing neural network API.
Backward evaluation must return weight gradients and must return input gradients only when input-gradient computation is enabled.
The neural network must support circuits with only input parameters, only weight parameters, both kinds of parameters, or no parameters.
VQR must be able to construct and train with the estimator-backed neural network when no quantum instance is supplied or when an estimator is supplied.
VQR must preserve its existing quantum-instance workflow and reject observable types that are incompatible with the selected execution path.

interface.Name: EstimatorQNN
interface.Input: constructor: circuit, estimator=None, observables=None, input_params=None, weight_params=None, gradient=None, input_gradients: bool = False
interface.Description: Estimator-primitive neural network for expectation-value outputs from parameterized circuits, exposing circuit, observables, input_params, weight_params, and input_gradients behavior.

interface.Name: EstimatorQNN.forward
interface.Description: Evaluates estimator expectation values for input data and weights.

interface.Name: EstimatorQNN.backward
interface.Description: Evaluates estimator-gradient backward results for input data and weights.

interface.Name: VQR
interface.Input: constructor: num_qubits=None, feature_map=None, ansatz=None, observable=None, loss='squared_error', optimizer=None, warm_start: bool = False, quantum_instance=None, initial_point=None, callback=None, estimator=None
interface.Description: Variational quantum regressor that can use either the existing quantum-instance path or an estimator-backed neural network and exposes feature_map, ansatz, and num_qubits.

interface.Name: VQR.fit
interface.Description: Fits the variational regressor on regression data using the configured neural network and optimizer.

interface.Name: VQR.score
interface.Description: Scores the fitted variational regressor on regression data.

problem_statement: Qiskit Machine Learning neural networks currently compute gradients with respect to input data whenever backward gradients are requested. This is unnecessary for many workflows and can add avoidable computation. Users need neural networks to skip input-data gradients by default while still allowing them to enable input-gradient computation when a workflow requires it.
requirements: Neural networks must expose whether gradients with respect to input data are computed during backward.
Input-gradient computation must be disabled by default.
Users must be able to enable and disable input-gradient computation through the exposed property.
When input gradients are disabled, backward must return no input gradient while still returning weight gradients where the network supports them.
Circuit-based, opflow-based, and two-layer neural-network workflows must follow the same disabled-input-gradient behavior.
Existing forward and backward shape behavior must remain compatible for neural networks.

interface.Name: NeuralNetwork
interface.Input: constructor: num_inputs, num_weights, sparse, sampling, output_shape
interface.Description: Base neural network initializes input-gradient computation as disabled by default.

interface.Name: NeuralNetwork.input_gradients
interface.Description: Property getter and setter expose whether backward computes gradients with respect to input data.

interface.Name: NeuralNetwork.backward
interface.Description: Runs the backward pass and returns input gradients only when input_gradients is enabled.

interface.Name: CircuitQNN
interface.Input: constructor: circuit, input_params=None, weight_params=None, sparse=False, sampling=False, interpret=None, output_shape=None, gradient=None, quantum_instance=None
interface.Description: Circuit neural network returns None for input gradients when input_gradients is disabled.

interface.Name: CircuitQNN.input_gradients
interface.Description: Property getter and setter control whether CircuitQNN backward computes gradients with respect to input data.

interface.Name: OpflowQNN
interface.Input: constructor: operator, input_params, weight_params, exp_val=None, gradient=None, quantum_instance=None
interface.Description: Opflow neural network returns None for input gradients when input_gradients is disabled.

interface.Name: OpflowQNN.input_gradients
interface.Description: Property getter and setter control whether OpflowQNN backward computes gradients with respect to input data.

interface.Name: TwoLayerQNN
interface.Input: constructor: num_qubits=None, feature_map=None, ansatz=None, observable=None, exp_val=None, quantum_instance=None
interface.Description: Two-layer neural network inherits the input-gradient toggle behavior of opflow neural networks.

problem_statement: Building quantum neural networks often requires composing a feature map circuit with an ansatz circuit and then passing both the composed circuit and the two parameter groups to the neural network. Users currently need to assemble this wrapper manually each time. The library should provide a reusable blueprint circuit that encapsulates this composition and exposes the input and weight parameters separately.
requirements: Provide a QNNCircuit blueprint circuit that composes a feature map followed by an ansatz.
QNNCircuit must be constructible from a number of qubits, a feature map, an ansatz, or a compatible combination of these inputs.
When no feature map is supplied, QNNCircuit must create a default feature map for the resolved number of qubits, using a single-qubit feature map when appropriate.
When no ansatz is supplied, QNNCircuit must create a default ansatz for the resolved number of qubits.
If an explicit number of qubits is supplied together with circuits of different sizes, QNNCircuit must reconcile the feature map and ansatz to the explicit number of qubits when possible.
Updating the number of qubits, feature map, or ansatz after construction must invalidate and reconfigure the blueprint circuit so that the stored circuits remain consistent.
QNNCircuit must expose the feature-map parameters as input parameters and the ansatz parameters as weight parameters.
QNNCircuit must be importable from the circuit library package.

interface.Name: QNNCircuit
interface.Input: constructor: num_qubits: int | None = None, feature_map: QuantumCircuit | None = None, ansatz: QuantumCircuit | None = None
interface.Description: Blueprint circuit that wraps a feature map and ansatz into one composed circuit, exposes num_qubits, feature_map, ansatz, input_parameters, and weight_parameters, updates component circuit sizes through setters, raises QiskitMachineLearningError for invalid construction, and preserves these properties under copy.

interface.Name: QNNCircuit._build
interface.Description: Builds the blueprint circuit by composing the resolved feature map followed by the resolved ansatz.

problem_statement: The repository already provides quantum kernel implementations, including a fidelity-based kernel and the older statevector-simulator workflow. However, users who want exact statevector-backed kernel evaluation still need an implementation that is optimized around direct statevector feature-map simulation and avoids repeated statevector computation. The repository should provide a dedicated statevector-backed fidelity kernel that fits the existing kernel API while reducing redundant computation through caching.
requirements: A dedicated statevector-backed fidelity kernel must be available through the public kernel API.
The kernel must evaluate symmetric and asymmetric kernel matrices from one-dimensional or two-dimensional input data.
The returned kernel values must match the previous statevector-simulator kernel behavior for supported feature maps, including duplicate samples.
The kernel must work with default feature-map behavior and must adjust the feature-map size consistently with the existing base kernel validation rules.
The kernel must support a caller-provided statevector implementation compatible with the configured feature map.
Statevectors computed during evaluation must be cached so duplicate samples do not require redundant statevector computation.
The cache must support automatic clearing on evaluation by default, optional retention across evaluations, an optional maximum size, and explicit clearing by the caller.

interface.Name: FidelityStatevectorKernel
interface.Input: constructor: feature_map=None, statevector_type=Statevector, cache_size=None, auto_clear_cache: bool = True
interface.Description: Statevector-backed fidelity kernel with configurable feature map, statevector implementation, statevector cache behavior, and feature_map and num_features properties.

interface.Name: FidelityStatevectorKernel.evaluate
interface.Description: Evaluates symmetric or asymmetric fidelity kernel matrices from statevector feature-map simulations.

interface.Name: FidelityStatevectorKernel.clear_cache
interface.Description: Clears the cached statevectors used during kernel evaluation.

interface.Name: FidelityStatevectorKernel._get_statevector
interface.Description: Returns a cached statevector for bound feature-map parameter values and exposes cache statistics used to verify cache behavior.

interface.Name: FidelityStatevectorKernel._compute_kernel_entry
interface.Description: Computes a single statevector fidelity entry and can be wrapped by tests to verify duplicate-sample caching behavior.

problem_statement: The repository already provides FidelityStatevectorKernel as an optimized statevector-backed kernel implementation. It computes exact fidelities from statevectors, but users who want to approximate the sampling noise of fidelity measurements do not have a way to emulate finite-shot behavior in this kernel. The kernel should support optional shot-noise emulation while preserving exact behavior by default.
requirements: FidelityStatevectorKernel must support exact fidelity evaluation when no shot count is provided.
FidelityStatevectorKernel must accept a finite shot count and use it to emulate sampling noise in each fidelity value.
Shot-noise emulation must sample from a binomial distribution whose probability is the exact fidelity and return the sampled mean.
The kernel must support disabling positive-semidefinite correction when finite-shot noise is used.
When positive-semidefinite correction is enabled for a symmetric kernel matrix with finite-shot noise, the returned matrix must be projected to a positive-semidefinite matrix.
Existing default construction, exact kernel evaluation, and statevector cache behavior must remain compatible with the previous API.

interface.Name: FidelityStatevectorKernel
interface.Input: constructor: feature_map=None, statevector_type=Statevector, cache_size=None, auto_clear_cache: bool = True, shots: int | None = None, enforce_psd: bool = True
interface.Description: Statevector-backed fidelity kernel whose constructor supports optional finite-shot noise emulation and PSD enforcement control.

interface.Name: FidelityStatevectorKernel.evaluate
interface.Description: Evaluates symmetric or asymmetric fidelity kernel matrices, including optional shot-noise emulation and PSD correction.

interface.Name: FidelityStatevectorKernel._compute_kernel_entry
interface.Description: Computes one fidelity kernel entry, using exact fidelity or finite-shot sampling as configured.

problem_statement: The repository already provides SamplerQNN and EstimatorQNN implementations that operate on parameterized circuits, and it also provides QNNCircuit as a higher-level wrapper around feature-map and ansatz circuits. However, users still had to manually pass separate input and weight parameter lists when constructing SamplerQNN or EstimatorQNN, even when those parameters were already tracked by a QNNCircuit. The QNN interfaces should accept QNNCircuit directly and infer the required parameter lists from it.
requirements: SamplerQNN must accept a QNNCircuit as its circuit argument and derive input_params from the QNNCircuit input parameters.
SamplerQNN must derive weight_params from the QNNCircuit weight parameters when a QNNCircuit is provided.
EstimatorQNN must accept a QNNCircuit as its circuit argument and derive input_params from the QNNCircuit input parameters.
EstimatorQNN must derive weight_params from the QNNCircuit weight parameters when a QNNCircuit is provided.
Constructing either QNN from an equivalent manually composed circuit with explicit parameters or from a QNNCircuit must produce matching parameter properties.
Forward and backward evaluations for the QNNCircuit-based construction must match the equivalent manually composed circuit construction.

interface.Description: Evaluates the sampler neural network forward pass for explicit circuits and QNNCircuit-based construction.

problem_statement: Neural-network classifier workflows currently require users to provide numeric or one-hot encoded target labels. Users should be able to train and score neural-network classifiers, including VQC-style classifiers, with categorical string labels directly while preserving the existing one_hot behavior.
requirements: NeuralNetworkClassifier must accept categorical string target labels in fit and score.
Categorical labels must be detected from string target data and encoded before training or scoring.
When one_hot is true, categorical labels must be encoded as one-hot target data.
When one_hot is false, categorical labels must be encoded as integer class labels.
Categorical label handling must work with absolute error, squared error, and cross entropy classifier losses where applicable.
Existing numeric-label classifier behavior must remain compatible.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkClassifier
interface.Input: constructor: neural_network, loss='squared_error', one_hot=False, optimizer=None, warm_start=False, initial_point=None, callback=None
interface.Description: Classifier that accepts categorical string target labels and encodes them according to one_hot during fit and score.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkClassifier.fit
interface.Description: Fits the classifier after encoding categorical string labels when present.

interface.Name: NeuralNetworkClassifier.score
interface.Description: Scores the classifier after applying the fitted categorical label encoder when needed.

problem_statement: The repository already provides a trainable fidelity quantum kernel for the primitive-based kernel stack, and it also provides a statevector-based fidelity kernel for kernel evaluation. However, there is no trainable statevector-based counterpart. Users who want statevector-backed kernel evaluation cannot train that kernel through the same workflow used by the existing trainable fidelity kernel. The repository should support a trainable statevector kernel that fits naturally into the existing trainable kernel workflow.
requirements: The statevector-backed trainable kernel must accept the same trainable-kernel configuration style as the existing trainable fidelity kernel, including a feature map and explicit training parameters.
It must expose training-parameter and feature counts consistently with the existing trainable kernel API.
It must support valid training-parameter assignment through mappings, lists, and NumPy arrays, including partial reassignment, while rejecting wrong-sized or invalid assignments.

After all training parameters are bound, it must evaluate symmetric and asymmetric kernel matrices correctly; if required training parameters remain unbound, evaluation must raise the repository's machine-learning error.
