interface.Input: constructor: feature_map=None, statevector_type=Statevector, training_parameters=None, cache_size=None, auto_clear_cache: bool = True, shots=None, enforce_psd: bool = True
interface.Description: Trainable statevector-based fidelity kernel exposing assigned parameter_values, training_parameters, num_training_parameters, and num_features.

interface.Name: TrainableFidelityStatevectorKernel.assign_training_parameters
interface.Description: Assigns trainable kernel parameter values from mappings, lists, or NumPy arrays, including partial reassignment.

interface.Name: TrainableFidelityStatevectorKernel.evaluate
interface.Description: Evaluates symmetric or asymmetric statevector-backed trainable fidelity kernel matrices after all training parameters are bound.

problem_statement: Neural-network classifier and regressor training still contains places that process samples one at a time even though the neural network implementations can evaluate batches. Users need the underlying loss handling to preserve per-sample behavior for batched predictions and targets so training objectives can consume batches without collapsing them into a single scalar loss too early.
requirements: For one-dimensional batched inputs, L1 and L2 loss evaluation must return one loss value per sample instead of collapsing the entire batch into one scalar.
L1 and L2 loss gradients must preserve the input prediction shape and match the elementwise gradient of the corresponding loss.
Existing neural-network classifier and regressor workflows using L1 and L2-style losses must continue to run after the batched loss behavior is added.

interface.Name: L1Loss
interface.Description: Provides L1 loss evaluation and gradients for one-dimensional batched arrays.

interface.Name: L1Loss.evaluate
interface.Description: Returns absolute-error losses with one value per sample for one-dimensional batched predictions.

interface.Name: L1Loss.gradient
interface.Description: Returns the elementwise L1 gradient with the same shape as the prediction input.

interface.Name: L2Loss
interface.Description: Provides squared-error loss evaluation and gradients for one-dimensional batched arrays.

interface.Name: L2Loss.evaluate
interface.Description: Returns squared-error losses with one value per sample for one-dimensional batched predictions.

interface.Name: L2Loss.gradient
interface.Description: Returns the elementwise L2 gradient with the same shape as the prediction input.

problem_statement: Users of Qiskit Machine Learning neural networks need direct control over whether gradients with respect to input data are computed. The existing API only exposes this as mutable state after construction, and connector workflows should work with neural networks whose input-gradient behavior was explicitly chosen by the user.
requirements: Neural networks must accept an optional input-gradient flag during construction, with input gradients disabled by default.
The input-gradient property must reflect the constructor value and remain configurable through the existing property setter.
Circuit-based neural network constructors must expose the same input-gradient choice and propagate it to backward-gradient computation.
Opflow-based neural network constructors must expose the same input-gradient choice and propagate it to backward-gradient computation.
Two-layer neural network construction must expose the input-gradient choice through its public constructor.
Torch connector autograd workflows must continue to operate when a neural network is constructed with input gradients explicitly enabled.
Existing forward and backward output-shape behavior must remain unchanged when input gradients are left at their default setting.

interface.Name: NeuralNetwork
interface.Input: constructor: num_inputs, num_weights, sparse, output_shape, input_gradients=False
interface.Description: Base neural network constructor accepts an optional boolean controlling whether backward computes gradients with respect to input data.

interface.Name: NeuralNetwork.input_gradients
interface.Description: Property getter and setter expose whether input gradients are computed by backward.

interface.Description: Circuit neural network constructor accepts input_gradients and uses it for backward input-gradient behavior.

interface.Description: Two-layer neural network constructor forwards input_gradients to the underlying opflow neural network.

interface.Name: TorchConnector
interface.Description: Torch connector wraps a neural network whose input-gradient behavior was configured before connector construction.

interface.Name: TorchConnector._TorchNNFunction.apply
interface.Description: Autograd entry point must support gradient checking when the wrapped neural network has input gradients enabled.

problem_statement: The repository provides several optimizers backed by NLopt, including CRS, DIRECT_L, DIRECT_L_RAND, ESCH, and ISRES. However, it does not currently include support for the SBPLX optimizer. Users who rely on the existing NLopt optimizer family cannot use SBPLX through the same optimizer workflow. The repository should support SBPLX consistently with the other NLopt-backed optimizers.
requirements: The new optimizer must integrate with the existing NLopt-backed optimizer family, be exported through the same public __init__.py modules as the other NLopt optimizers, be importable both as qiskit_machine_learning.optimizers.SBPLX and from the NLopt optimizer package, and identify SBPLX as the local NLopt LN_SBPLX backend through the repository's NLopt optimizer type protocol.
It must support the standard optimizer workflow, including option setting, optional bounds, and minimization behavior consistent with the other NLopt-backed optimizers.

interface.Name: SBPLX
interface.Description: NLopt-based Subplex optimizer.

interface.Name: SBPLX.get_nlopt_optimizer
interface.Description: Returns the NLopt backend associated with SBPLX.

interface.Name: SBPLX.set_options
interface.Description: Updates optimizer options such as max_evals for the SBPLX optimizer workflow.

interface.Name: SBPLX.minimize
interface.Description: Runs SBPLX minimization with optional bounds through the existing NLopt optimizer workflow.

problem_statement: The repository supports kernel-based training for classification through an SVC-oriented loss, but it does not provide corresponding regression-oriented kernel loss functions. As a result, the kernel trainer cannot be used naturally for regression workflows such as support-vector regression, even though the repository already has trainable kernel and trainer abstractions for this kind of workflow. The repository should support regression-focused kernel losses that integrate with the existing training flow.
requirements: The new regression losses must follow the existing kernel-loss evaluation protocol so they can be used by the kernel trainer with trainable quantum kernels, training data, and regression labels.
They must support regression-oriented fitting based on support-vector-regression-style kernel training.
Training with any of the new regression losses must produce concrete bound training-parameter values on the resulting quantum kernel.
A quantum kernel trained with any of the new regression losses must be usable by the repository's quantum support-vector regressor for fitting and scoring regression data, producing finite scores.

interface.Description: Evaluates the mean squared regression kernel loss.

interface.Description: Evaluates the mean absolute regression kernel loss.

interface.Name: HuberLoss
interface.Description: Huber regression kernel loss.

interface.Name: HuberLoss.evaluate
interface.Description: Evaluates the Huber regression kernel loss.

problem_statement: The second-quantization operator stack already supports fermionic, bosonic, spin, and vibrational operators, but it does not provide a standalone representation for Majorana fermion operators. This prevents users from expressing Majorana terms directly and from using Majorana operators as a foundation for Majorana-based mappers and related transformations. The repository should support a first-class Majorana operator that works consistently with the existing sparse operator algebra.
requirements: The new operator must represent weighted sums of Majorana terms using sparse labels with underscore-prefixed mode indices.
Construction must support explicit mode counts, automatic mode-count inference, optional validation skipping, and optional by-reference storage of input data.
Invalid labels or labels whose indices exceed the declared mode count must raise the repository's standard operator validation error when validation is enabled.

The operator must preserve existing sparse-label operator semantics for scalar arithmetic, addition, subtraction, composition, tensoring, expansion, powers, adjoints, equivalence checks, and induced norms.
Simplification must cancel repeated Majorana factors within a label without reordering labels, while index ordering must produce equivalent terms ordered by mode index with the correct sign changes.
The operator must support parameterized coefficients where existing sparse-label arithmetic supports them, and hermiticity checks must reject parameterized operators.
The operator must convert to and from structured term iterators without changing the represented operator.
The operator must be constructible from polynomial tensor data whose keys consist only of Majorana placeholders.

The operator must be constructible from fermionic operators using the standard Majorana convention, with the resulting mode count twice the fermionic spin-orbital count and with caller-controlled simplification behavior.
Mode-index permutation must return an equivalent operator over the same mode count with every term index remapped by the provided permutation.
The operator must be available from the public second-quantized operators API.

interface.Name: MajoranaOp
interface.Input: constructor: data: Mapping[str, coeff], num_modes: int | None = None, copy: bool = True, validate: bool = True
interface.Description: Sparse-label operator representing weighted Majorana fermion terms, including inferred num_modes/register_length, configurable tolerance attributes, arithmetic operations, exact equality, composition with @, tensor product with ^, and power behavior.

interface.Description: Constructs a Majorana operator from structured term and coefficient pairs.

interface.Description: Iterates over structured Majorana term and coefficient pairs.

interface.Description: Returns the composed Majorana operator.

interface.Name: MajoranaOp.tensor
interface.Description: Returns the tensor product with another Majorana operator.

interface.Name: MajoranaOp.expand
interface.Description: Returns the reversed tensor product with another Majorana operator.

interface.Name: MajoranaOp.transpose
interface.Description: Returns the transpose of the Majorana operator.

interface.Name: MajoranaOp.simplify
interface.Description: Returns an equivalent operator with repeated Majorana factors simplified within each label.

interface.Description: Returns an equivalent operator with each label ordered by mode index.

interface.Description: Returns whether the operator is Hermitian up to an absolute tolerance.

interface.Description: Returns whether two Majorana operators are equivalent within configured tolerances.

interface.Description: Returns the induced norm of the Majorana operator coefficients.

interface.Description: Returns an equivalent operator with every mode index remapped by the provided permutation.

interface.Description: Constructs the additive identity Majorana operator.

interface.Description: Constructs the multiplicative identity Majorana operator.

problem_statement: Qiskit Nature's second-quantized operator classes already support algebraic manipulation, adjoints, and reduction, but users still lack a direct way to ask whether a constructed operator is Hermitian. This makes it awkward to validate operator expressions before handing them to downstream algorithms. Second-quantized operators should expose a public hermiticity check that works consistently across the FermionicOp, SpinOp, and VibrationalOp families while preserving nearby operator behavior.
requirements: Provide a public hermiticity check for second-quantized operators.
The hermiticity check must be available on SecondQuantizedOp-based operator types including FermionicOp, SpinOp, and VibrationalOp.
Hermiticity checking must correctly account for reduced operator contents, including cases where equivalent terms appear multiple times before simplification.
Hermiticity checking must return true for representative Hermitian second-quantized operator expressions and false for representative non-Hermitian expressions across the supported operator families.
Existing nearby reduction, ladder-operator expansion, vibrational-label parsing, and operator addition behavior must remain compatible.

interface.Name: SecondQuantizedOp.is_hermitian
interface.Description: Returns whether the second-quantized operator is Hermitian after comparing its reduced terms against the reduced terms of its adjoint.

problem_statement: Second-quantized fermionic operators in Qiskit Nature already support symbolic algebra, but users still lack a direct way to turn a FermionicOp into its matrix representation on the full fermionic Fock space. This blocks straightforward spectral checks and matrix-based downstream workflows that are already available for related operator types. FermionicOp should expose a public to_matrix conversion that produces the operator matrix in occupation-number basis and preserves the existing nearby operator behavior.
requirements: FermionicOp must provide a public to_matrix conversion over the full fermionic Fock space in occupation-number basis.
The basis ordering used by to_matrix must be the increasing bitstring order of the occupation-number basis states.
FermionicOp.to_matrix must support returning either a sparse matrix representation or a dense numpy array.
The matrix representation must correctly handle identity, number, emptiness, creation, annihilation, and multi-term operators with fermionic sign conventions.
Matrix conversion for physically relevant fermionic Hamiltonian terms must preserve the expected spectrum and particle-number structure of the resulting states.
Existing FermionicOp multi-term construction, addition, matrix multiplication, reduction, and hermiticity behavior must remain compatible.

interface.Name: FermionicOp.to_matrix
interface.Description: Returns the full-Fock-space matrix representation of the fermionic operator in occupation-number basis, optionally as a dense array.

problem_statement: The repository already supports bosonic operators and provides a linear boson-to-qubit mapper. However, it does not provide a logarithmic boson-to-qubit mapping. This means bosonic modes currently require a number of qubits that scales linearly with the represented occupation space, which limits larger truncation levels and future mixed boson-fermion workflows. The repository should support a logarithmic mapper for bosonic operators.
requirements: The mapper must accept a maximum occupation value and use it to map each bosonic mode with logarithmic qubit scaling.
Calling the existing public mapper API on bosonic operator inputs must correctly translate creation and annihilation operators for single-mode and multi-mode cases.
The mapped qubit operators must have correct coefficients and qubit ordering for number-like terms, repeated operators, and cross-mode operator products.

interface.Name: BosonicLogarithmicMapper
interface.Description: Boson-to-qubit mapper using logarithmic local encoding.

interface.Name: BosonicLogarithmicMapper.map
interface.Description: Maps bosonic creation and annihilation operator inputs to qubit operators using logarithmic local encoding.

problem_statement: Qiskit Nature needs first-class second-quantized Property objects for core electronic observables instead of relying only on older problem-specific helpers. Users should be able to construct reusable ParticleNumber, Magnetization, and AngularMomentum properties from driver results and obtain the expected second-quantized operators from them.
requirements: Provide a second-quantized Property framework for reusable electronic observables in Qiskit Nature.
ParticleNumber must be constructible from an electronic driver result and expose the expected number-operator terms through second_q_ops().
Magnetization must be constructible from an electronic driver result and expose the expected spin-resolved magnetization terms through second_q_ops().
AngularMomentum must be constructible from an electronic driver result and expose the expected second-quantized angular-momentum operator through second_q_ops().
Existing electronic-structure problem operator generation and downstream operator-evaluation behavior must remain compatible.

interface.Name: SecondQuantizedProperty
interface.Input: constructor: property metadata defined by subclasses
interface.Description: Base contract for reusable second-quantized property objects that can be built from driver results and converted into second-quantized operators.

interface.Name: SecondQuantizedProperty.from_driver_result
interface.Description: Constructs a property instance from a supported electronic or vibrational driver result.

interface.Name: SecondQuantizedProperty.second_q_ops
interface.Description: Returns the second-quantized operators represented by the property.

interface.Name: ParticleNumber
interface.Description: Represents the particle-number observable as a reusable electronic property.

interface.Name: ParticleNumber.from_driver_result
interface.Description: Constructs the particle-number property from an electronic driver result.

interface.Name: Magnetization
interface.Description: Represents the electronic magnetization observable as a reusable property.

interface.Name: Magnetization.from_driver_result
interface.Description: Constructs the magnetization property from an electronic driver result.

interface.Name: AngularMomentum
interface.Description: Represents the electronic angular-momentum observable as a reusable property.

interface.Name: AngularMomentum.from_driver_result
interface.Description: Constructs the angular-momentum property from an electronic driver result.

problem_statement: Electronic-structure results do not currently provide a built-in way to recover electronic charge-density information. Users who want one- and two-particle reduced density matrices have to reconstruct them manually instead of requesting them through the second-quantized properties stack. The repository should provide an ElectronicDensity property that can be attached to an electronic-structure problem, translated into auxiliary operators, and interpreted back onto the result object.
requirements: The second-quantized properties package must expose an ElectronicDensity property for electronic-structure workflows.
ElectronicDensity must be constructible from alpha and beta orbital occupations and produce the corresponding one- and two-particle density integrals.
ElectronicDensity must expose second-quantized auxiliary operators for the stored reduced-density data.
ElectronicDensity must be able to interpret evaluated auxiliary-operator results and attach the reconstructed density information to an ElectronicStructureResult.
Existing electronic-properties container behavior for other properties and existing ElectronicIntegrals behavior unrelated to density reconstruction must remain compatible.

interface.Name: ElectronicDensity
interface.Description: Represents electronic one- and two-particle density information in the second-quantized properties stack.

interface.Name: ElectronicDensity.from_orbital_occupation
interface.Description: Constructs an ElectronicDensity instance from alpha and beta orbital occupations.

interface.Name: ElectronicDensity.second_q_ops
interface.Description: Builds the auxiliary second-quantized operators needed to evaluate the stored reduced-density quantities.

interface.Name: ElectronicDensity.interpret
interface.Description: Reads evaluated auxiliary-operator values and stores the reconstructed electronic density on the ElectronicStructureResult.

problem_statement: Qiskit Nature already provides fermionic second-quantized operators, but spin-model workflows still lack a modern spin operator abstraction that users can build from intuitive labels and convert into matrix form for downstream quantum simulations and mappings. Users should be able to construct spin operators from dense and sparse spin labels, use raising and lowering labels naturally, and obtain matrices that match the expected spin algebra.
requirements: The repository must expose a SpinOp operator from qiskit_nature.operators for spin-model workflows.
SpinOp must accept dense and sparse spin labels built from I, X, Y, Z, +, and - symbols.
SpinOp must support multi-register labels and preserve the expected register ordering when constructed from dense or sparse labels.
SpinOp must interpret + and - labels as the corresponding raising and lowering combinations of X and Y operators.
SpinOp.to_matrix must return the correct matrix representation for supported single-spin and multi-spin label constructions.
SpinOp matrix behavior for qubit-spin labels must stay consistent with the corresponding Pauli matrices.
Existing nearby FermionicOp algebra behavior must remain compatible.

interface.Name: SpinOp
interface.Description: Represents a spin operator built from dense labels, sparse labels, or internal spin-array data.

interface.Name: SpinOp.to_matrix
interface.Description: Returns the dense matrix representation of the constructed spin operator.

problem_statement: Qiskit Nature needs a modular electronic driver-result representation so that electronic integrals can be grouped into reusable property objects instead of being handled only as ad hoc raw arrays. Users should be able to organize one-body and two-body electronic integrals inside an IntegralProperty, query them by basis and body rank, transform their basis consistently, and generate the corresponding second-quantized operator.
requirements: Provide a reusable IntegralProperty abstraction for electronic integrals in Qiskit Nature's property framework.
IntegralProperty must store electronic integrals grouped by electronic basis and number of body terms.
IntegralProperty must allow querying stored integrals by basis and body rank and return None when a requested entry is unavailable.
Applying an electronic basis transform to IntegralProperty must update or extend the stored integrals consistently for the transformed basis.
IntegralProperty.second_q_ops() must build the expected fermionic operator from the stored electronic integrals.

interface.Name: IntegralProperty
interface.Description: Groups electronic integrals into a reusable electronic property that can be transformed and converted into second-quantized operators.

interface.Name: IntegralProperty.add_electronic_integral
interface.Description: Adds an electronic-integral object into the property's internal storage keyed by basis and body rank.

interface.Name: IntegralProperty.get_electronic_integral
interface.Description: Returns the stored electronic integrals for a requested basis and body rank when available.

interface.Name: IntegralProperty.transform_basis
interface.Description: Transforms the stored electronic integrals into the target electronic basis and keeps them accessible through the property.

interface.Name: IntegralProperty.second_q_ops
interface.Description: Builds the second-quantized operator represented by the currently stored electronic integrals.

problem_statement: The protein-folding module forbids attaching a side chain to the second bead of the main chain in order to save one qubit in the encoded optimization problem. That restriction prevents users from modeling proteins whose second main bead actually has a side chain. The repository should support that configuration while still keeping the existing qubit-saving behavior for proteins that do not use a second-bead side chain.
requirements: Protein-folding peptide construction must allow a side chain on the second main bead while continuing to reject side chains on the first and last main beads.
When the second main bead has a side chain, the qubit-fixing logic must preserve the additional qubit needed to encode that configuration instead of applying the old fixed-qubit reduction.
ProteinFoldingProblem must produce the expected qubit operator for proteins whose second main bead has a side chain.
Existing protein-folding behavior for inputs without a second-bead side chain must remain compatible.
Existing invalid-side-chain checks for the first and last main beads must remain compatible.

interface.Name: Peptide
interface.Description: Builds the protein-folding peptide model and must accept a side chain on the second main bead while still rejecting side chains on the first and last main beads.

interface.Name: ProteinFoldingProblem
interface.Description: Creates the protein-folding optimization problem for a peptide, including cases where the second main bead has a side chain.

interface.Name: ProteinFoldingProblem._qubit_op_full
interface.Description: Builds the full qubit operator and must produce the expected operator when the second main bead has a side chain.

interface.Name: _fix_qubits
interface.Description: Applies the fixed-qubit reduction and must preserve the additional encoded qubit when the second main bead has a side chain.

problem_statement: When a ParityMapper-backed QubitConverter is configured with two-qubit reduction, converting very small fermionic operators can produce a qubit operator with two or fewer qubits. The converter currently still attempts two-qubit reduction in that situation, which can surface an IndexError from the underlying tapering machinery instead of returning a valid qubit operator. The converter should avoid applying two-qubit reduction when the mapped operator is already too small for that reduction.
requirements: QubitConverter must leave two-qubit-or-smaller mapped operators unchanged when two-qubit reduction is requested.
The converter must emit a warning when it skips a requested two-qubit reduction because the mapped operator contains two or fewer qubits.
Converting a two-or-fewer-qubit FermionicOp through a ParityMapper-backed QubitConverter with two_qubit_reduction enabled must return the expected unreduced PauliSumOp rather than raising IndexError.
Existing ParityMapper behavior, including its advertised support for two-qubit reduction and standard mapping output, must remain compatible.
Existing FermionicOp construction, arithmetic, scalar multiplication, and reduction behavior must remain compatible.

interface.Name: QubitConverter
interface.Description: Converts second-quantized operators to qubit operators while honoring two-qubit reduction settings.

interface.Name: QubitConverter.convert
interface.Description: Maps an operator and applies compatible reductions, skipping two-qubit reduction for operators with two or fewer qubits.

interface.Name: ParityMapper
interface.Description: Mapper used by QubitConverter that supports parity mapping and two-qubit reduction.

interface.Name: FermionicOp
interface.Description: Second-quantized fermionic operator accepted by QubitConverter and used for small-operator conversion.

problem_statement: Two-body electronic integral tensors are expected in chemists' notation in the second-quantized operator stack, but users and upstream chemistry tooling may also produce the same tensor data in physicists' notation or another equivalent intermediate ordering. Users need reliable utilities to identify the ordering of a four-dimensional two-body integral tensor and convert it into chemists' or physicists' ordering without manually transposing axes.
requirements: The second-quantized operators package must provide utilities for detecting the index ordering of rank-four two-body electronic integral tensors.
The ordering detector must distinguish chemists' ordering, physicists' ordering, a supported intermediate ordering, and unknown ordering.
A tensor already in the requested target ordering must be returned with equivalent values.
A tensor in chemists' ordering or the supported intermediate ordering must be convertible to physicists' ordering.
A tensor in physicists' ordering or the supported intermediate ordering must be convertible to chemists' ordering.
Conversion functions must raise a QiskitNatureError when the input ordering cannot be identified as one of the supported two-body integral orderings.
Existing PolynomialTensor initialization, lookup, iteration, scalar multiplication, addition, conjugation, and transposition behavior must remain compatible.

interface.Name: IndexType
interface.Description: Enum describing supported two-body tensor index orderings, including chemists', physicists', intermediate, and unknown ordering.

interface.Name: find_index_order
interface.Description: Identifies the index ordering of a rank-four two-body electronic integral tensor.

interface.Name: to_chemist_ordering
interface.Description: Returns a two-body electronic integral tensor in chemists' ordering or raises QiskitNatureError when the input ordering is unsupported.

interface.Name: to_physicist_ordering
interface.Description: Returns a two-body electronic integral tensor in physicists' ordering or raises QiskitNatureError when the input ordering is unsupported.

problem_statement: Minimum eigensolver factories make it convenient to construct VQE-based solvers for electronic and vibrational structure problems, but they do not expose VQE's callback hook. Users who need to observe optimization progress, collect intermediate energies, or monitor long hardware-backed runs cannot pass a callback through these factories. The factories should support the same callback behavior as VQE while keeping their existing solver construction behavior.
requirements: VQEUCCFactory must accept an optional callback argument and expose it through a callback property.
VQEUVCCFactory must accept an optional callback argument and expose it through a callback property.
When either factory constructs a VQE solver, the configured callback must be passed to that VQE so it is invoked during optimization with the VQE callback arguments.
Additional keyword arguments supplied to the VQE-based factories must be forwarded to the constructed VQE solver.
Existing VQEUCCFactory and VQEUVCCFactory solver construction, ansatz setup, initial state handling, optimizer configuration, and energy calculation behavior must remain compatible.

interface.Name: VQEUCCFactory
interface.Input: constructor: quantum_instance, optimizer=None, initial_point=None, gradient=None, expectation=None, include_custom=False, ansatz=None, initial_state=None, callback=None, **kwargs

interface.Name: VQEUCCFactory.get_solver

interface.Name: VQEUVCCFactory
interface.Input: constructor: quantum_instance, optimizer=None, initial_point=None, gradient=None, expectation=None, include_custom=False, ansatz=None, initial_state=None, callback=None, **kwargs
interface.Description: Constructs a VQE UVCC minimum eigensolver factory while preserving callback and extra VQE keyword arguments for solver creation.

interface.Name: VQEUVCCFactory.callback
interface.Description: Gets or sets the callback passed to VQE solvers created by the factory.

interface.Name: VQEUVCCFactory.get_solver
interface.Description: Returns a VQE configured for the vibrational structure problem, including the factory callback and forwarded VQE keyword arguments.

problem_statement: Qiskit Nature's second-quantized fermionic workflows still depend on older primitive-style operator building blocks, which makes it awkward to construct and manipulate fermionic operators directly from compact labels. Users should have a modern FermionicOp abstraction that can be created from label data, supports the core fermionic operator algebra directly, and is available from the high-level qiskit_nature.operators package.
requirements: The repository must expose a FermionicOp class from qiskit_nature.operators.
FermionicOp must accept valid fermionic labels and multi-term label-coefficient input data.
FermionicOp must reject invalid label input with a QiskitNatureError.
FermionicOp must support scalar multiplication and operator addition over label-based terms.
FermionicOp must support fermionic operator composition with the @ operator and preserve the expected fermionic sign behavior.
FermionicOp.reduce must merge duplicate labels and keep the resulting coefficients consistent with fermionic operator algebra.
Existing nearby FermionicOperator transformation and mapping behavior must remain compatible.

interface.Name: FermionicOp
interface.Description: Represents a label-based fermionic operator and supports scalar multiplication, addition, and composition through Python operator syntax.

interface.Name: FermionicOp.reduce
interface.Description: Merges duplicate fermionic labels and removes coefficients that are numerically zero within the configured tolerances.

problem_statement: Qiskit Nature can already build fermionic operators and apply electronic-structure transformations, but users still lack a higher-level molecular problem object that runs a driver, applies optional transformers, and returns the corresponding second-quantized operators needed by downstream algorithms. Users should be able to construct a MolecularProblem from a fermionic driver, request its second-quantized operators with or without an active-space reduction, and receive the expected electronic and auxiliary operators in a stable order.
requirements: Provide a MolecularProblem abstraction for molecular second-quantization workflows.
MolecularProblem must accept a fermionic driver together with an optional list of QMolecule transformers.
MolecularProblem.second_q_ops must run the driver, apply the configured transformers, and return the resulting second-quantized operators in a stable order.
Without transformers, MolecularProblem.second_q_ops must include the expected electronic operator together with the standard auxiliary molecular operators and, when available, dipole operators.
With an active-space transformer, MolecularProblem.second_q_ops must return the reduced electronic operator and corresponding reduced auxiliary operator set for the active space.
Existing ActiveSpaceTransformer behavior and nearby FermionicOp algebra behavior must remain compatible.

interface.Name: MolecularProblem
interface.Description: Represents a molecular second-quantization problem built from a fermionic driver and optional QMolecule transformers.

interface.Name: MolecularProblem.second_q_ops
interface.Description: Runs the configured driver workflow and returns the electronic, auxiliary, and optional dipole second-quantized operators in the expected order.

problem_statement: Qiskit Nature can already load molecular electronic-structure data into a QMolecule, but users still lack a reusable active-space reduction utility that trims a molecule down to a chosen subset of orbitals and electrons before downstream algorithm steps. Users should be able to configure an active-space transformer, apply it to QMolecule instances loaded from HDF5 data, and obtain reduced integrals together with the correct electron counts and accumulated inactive-space energy shift.
requirements: Provide an ActiveSpaceTransformer abstraction for QMolecule-based active-space reduction workflows.
ActiveSpaceTransformer must accept the configured number of active electrons and orbitals, and optionally a separate number of active alpha electrons or an explicit list of active orbital indices.

ActiveSpaceTransformer.transform must reduce a QMolecule to the requested active space and return a new QMolecule containing the reduced molecular-orbital integrals and updated orbital and particle counts.
When the requested active space matches the full space, the returned QMolecule must preserve the original molecular-orbital integrals and record a zero ActiveSpaceTransformer energy shift.

When reducing to a smaller active space, the returned QMolecule must expose the expected reduced one- and two-electron integrals together with the correct inactive-space energy shift under the ActiveSpaceTransformer key.
ActiveSpaceTransformer must support QMolecule inputs that do not provide mo_occ by constructing the occupation information from the molecular electron counts.
Existing HDF5Driver loading and QMolecule save-load behavior for nearby molecular integral data must remain compatible.

interface.Name: ActiveSpaceTransformer
interface.Description: Represents a configurable active-space reduction over QMolecule instances.

interface.Name: ActiveSpaceTransformer.transform
interface.Description: Returns a reduced QMolecule whose active-space integrals, particle counts, orbital counts, and ActiveSpaceTransformer energy shift match the configured reduction.

problem_statement: Qiskit Nature currently lacks a dedicated data structure for quadratic fermionic Hamiltonians, even though these Hamiltonians are naturally represented by Hermitian and antisymmetric coefficient matrices and need linear-algebra-based diagonalization routines. Users need a public QuadraticHamiltonian abstraction that stores those matrix blocks directly, exposes whether particle number is conserved, converts back to FermionicOp form, and computes the Bogoliubov transform that diagonalizes the Hamiltonian.
requirements: Provide a public QuadraticHamiltonian class in the second-quantization operators package.
QuadraticHamiltonian construction must accept a Hermitian particle-number-conserving matrix part, an antisymmetric pairing matrix part, an additive constant, and an optional num_modes override.
When either matrix block is omitted, QuadraticHamiltonian must fill the missing block with zeros of the inferred size, and it must reject inputs when neither matrix block nor num_modes is specified.
QuadraticHamiltonian must validate Hermitian and antisymmetric inputs by default, including shape consistency with each other and with num_modes, while allowing validation to be disabled explicitly.
QuadraticHamiltonian must expose the stored Hermitian block, antisymmetric block, constant, and inferred number of modes for later inspection.
QuadraticHamiltonian must report whether the Hamiltonian conserves particle number based on whether the antisymmetric block is zero.
QuadraticHamiltonian must convert itself into an equivalent FermionicOp representation with the correct one-body, pairing, and constant terms.

QuadraticHamiltonian must provide the Majorana-form and diagonalizing Bogoliubov transform needed to diagonalize both particle-number-conserving and nonconserving quadratic Hamiltonians, returning sorted orbital energies and the transformed constant.
Existing FermionicOp construction, term iteration, register-length inference, arithmetic, matrix multiplication, and matrix-conversion behavior must remain compatible.

interface.Name: QuadraticHamiltonian
interface.Input: constructor: hermitian_part=None, antisymmetric_part=None, constant=0.0, num_modes=None, validate=True, rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-8
interface.Description: Represents a quadratic fermionic Hamiltonian using Hermitian and antisymmetric matrix blocks plus an additive constant.

interface.Name: QuadraticHamiltonian.hermitian_part
interface.Description: Returns the matrix of particle-number-conserving coefficients.

interface.Name: QuadraticHamiltonian.antisymmetric_part
interface.Description: Returns the matrix of pairing coefficients.

interface.Name: QuadraticHamiltonian.constant
interface.Description: Returns the additive constant term.

interface.Name: QuadraticHamiltonian.num_modes
interface.Description: Returns the number of fermionic modes represented by the Hamiltonian.

interface.Name: QuadraticHamiltonian.conserves_particle_number
interface.Description: Reports whether the antisymmetric block is zero and particle number is conserved.

interface.Name: QuadraticHamiltonian.to_fermionic_op
interface.Description: Converts the quadratic Hamiltonian into an equivalent FermionicOp.

interface.Name: QuadraticHamiltonian.majorana_form
interface.Description: Returns the real antisymmetric Majorana matrix and its associated constant term.

interface.Name: QuadraticHamiltonian.diagonalizing_bogoliubov_transform
interface.Description: Returns the transformation that diagonalizes the quadratic Hamiltonian, the sorted orbital energies, and the transformed constant.

problem_statement: Lattice currently accepts retworkx graph objects, but many users already build graph structures with networkx because it provides a broader set of graph generators and utilities. Users need to be able to construct a Lattice directly from a networkx.Graph without manually converting it first, while keeping the existing retworkx-based behavior intact.
requirements: Lattice construction must accept a networkx.Graph instance as input.
When a networkx.Graph is provided, the lattice must internally convert it into the graph representation used by existing Lattice behavior.
Unweighted networkx edges must be represented with the default unit edge weight after conversion.
The converted lattice graph must preserve the input graph's node and edge connectivity.
Existing Lattice construction and accessors for retworkx.PyGraph inputs must remain compatible.
Existing validation for invalid Lattice graph inputs, including nonnumeric edge weights, must remain compatible.

interface.Name: Lattice
interface.Description: Constructs a lattice from either a retworkx.PyGraph or a networkx.Graph while preserving node and edge connectivity.

interface.Name: Lattice.graph
interface.Description: Returns a copy of the lattice graph after construction.

problem_statement: Molecule currently assumes geometry coordinates are provided in Angstrom and does not let users declare the unit system used when constructing a molecule. This can make Bohr-coordinate inputs ambiguous and causes the molecule description to omit the unit context. Users need Molecule to accept an explicit coordinate unit and preserve that choice for later inspection and string rendering.
requirements: Molecule construction must accept an optional coordinate unit argument.
When no unit is provided, Molecule must continue to default to Angstrom units.
When UnitsType.ANGSTROM is provided explicitly, Molecule must preserve Angstrom as its unit without changing the supplied geometry.
When UnitsType.BOHR is provided, Molecule must preserve Bohr as its unit without changing the supplied geometry.
The units property must report the unit used for construction.
Existing Molecule construction, geometry, charge, multiplicity, stretching, bending, and perturbation behavior must remain compatible.

interface.Name: Molecule
interface.Input: constructor: geometry, multiplicity=1, charge=0, units=UnitsType.ANGSTROM, degrees_of_freedom=None, masses=None
interface.Description: Constructs a driver-independent molecule while preserving the coordinate unit used for the supplied geometry.

interface.Name: Molecule.units
interface.Description: Returns the coordinate unit stored on the molecule.

interface.Name: UnitsType
interface.Description: Provides the Angstrom and Bohr unit values accepted by Molecule construction and returned by Molecule.units.

problem_statement: Electronic-structure workflows can already reduce a problem to a user-chosen active space, but there is no dedicated transformer for the common freeze-core workflow. Users should be able to freeze chemically identified core orbitals, optionally remove additional unoccupied orbitals, and obtain the reduced QMolecule directly through a dedicated FreezeCoreTransformer instead of manually configuring an equivalent active-space reduction.
requirements: The repository must expose a dedicated FreezeCoreTransformer for reducing QMolecule instances by freezing core orbitals.
FreezeCoreTransformer must accept a freeze_core convenience setting that removes the QMolecule core orbitals and returns the expected reduced QMolecule.
When all orbitals remain active, FreezeCoreTransformer must preserve the original QMolecule data while keeping the expected transformer bookkeeping keys available for comparison.
FreezeCoreTransformer must accept an additional remove_orbitals list so users can remove extra unoccupied orbitals alongside the frozen core orbitals.
The reduced QMolecule produced by FreezeCoreTransformer must preserve the expected transformed integrals and energy-shift bookkeeping for the freeze-core reduction.
Existing ActiveSpaceTransformer behavior for manually configured active spaces must remain compatible.

interface.Name: FreezeCoreTransformer
interface.Description: Constructs a transformer that freezes QMolecule core orbitals and can additionally remove specified unoccupied orbitals.

interface.Name: FreezeCoreTransformer.transform
interface.Description: Reduces a QMolecule by freezing core orbitals, optionally removing additional unoccupied orbitals, and returning the transformed QMolecule.

problem_statement: FermionicOp currently accepts string-based labels, which works for hand-written operators but is awkward for code that generates fermionic operators programmatically. Users need to be able to construct FermionicOp terms from structured action/index label data without first formatting those labels as strings, while preserving the existing string-label behavior.
requirements: FermionicOp construction must accept terms whose labels are lists of action/index tuples.
Each tuple-based label element must use an action string such as + or - together with an integer fermionic mode index.
Tuple-based labels must produce the same dense and sparse operator content as equivalent string-based labels.
Register length must continue to be respected when tuple-based labels are supplied.
Existing FermionicOp initialization from dense labels, sparse string labels, multiple terms, scalar coefficients, and register length inference must remain compatible.

interface.Name: FermionicOp
interface.Description: Constructs a fermionic second-quantized operator from string labels or from list-of-tuple labels paired with coefficients.

interface.Name: FermionicOp.to_list
interface.Description: Returns the operator contents using the requested display format after any supported label input form has been normalized.

interface.Name: FermionicOp.register_length
interface.Description: Returns the register length used for dense conversion and operator storage.

problem_statement: FermionicOp can expose its terms through string-oriented helpers, but that format is awkward for programmatic access to creation and annihilation actions and their mode indices. Users need a supported way to iterate over the individual FermionicOp terms as structured action/index pairs together with each coefficient.
requirements: FermionicOp must provide a public terms iterator for individual operator terms.
Each yielded term must contain structured tuples of fermionic action symbols and integer mode indices together with the term coefficient.
Dense-format labels must be converted into the same structured sparse term representation used internally.
Existing FermionicOp initialization, register-length inference, scalar multiplication, and addition behavior must remain compatible.

interface.Name: FermionicOp.terms
interface.Description: Iterates over the FermionicOp terms, yielding each term as action/index pairs and its coefficient.

problem_statement: Qiskit Nature has lattice model Hamiltonians, but they cannot be used through the same problem abstraction workflow as electronic and vibrational structure problems. Users need a lattice model problem abstraction that wraps a lattice model Hamiltonian, exposes its second-quantized operators to solvers, and interprets raw eigensolver outputs as lattice-model results.
requirements: A lattice model problem must be constructible from a lattice model Hamiltonian.
The problem must expose the lattice model Hamiltonian through the standard second-quantized-operator entry point using the lattice energy as the main property.
The operator returned by the problem must match the operator produced by the wrapped lattice model.
Interpreting an EigenstateResult must preserve eigenenergies, eigenstates, and auxiliary-operator eigenvalues in a lattice model result.
Interpreting an EigensolverResult must convert eigenvalues, eigenstates, and auxiliary-operator eigenvalues into the corresponding lattice model result fields.
Interpreting a MinimumEigensolverResult must convert the scalar eigenvalue and eigenstate into one-element lattice-model result collections.
LatticeModelProblem must be importable from the second-quantization problems package.
LatticeModelResult must be importable from the results package.
Existing Fermi-Hubbard model construction and second-quantized operator behavior must remain compatible.

interface.Name: LatticeModelProblem
interface.Description: Wraps a lattice model Hamiltonian as a second-quantization problem with main property name LatticeEnergy.

interface.Name: LatticeModelProblem.second_q_ops
interface.Description: Returns the wrapped lattice model Hamiltonian operator under the problem's standard second-quantized-operator interface.

interface.Name: LatticeModelProblem.interpret
interface.Description: Converts EigenstateResult, EigensolverResult, or MinimumEigensolverResult data into a lattice model result.

interface.Name: LatticeModelResult
interface.Description: Stores interpreted lattice-model eigenstate data and computed lattice energies.

problem_statement: Qiskit Nature's VQE UCC workflow does not preserve a Hartree-Fock-compatible default initial point when users rely on the built-in factory behavior. Users who construct a VQE UCC ground-state solver without supplying an explicit initial point need the factory to provide a reusable Hartree-Fock initial-point object so the default parameterization remains the all-zero UCC point associated with an HF initial state.
requirements: Provide an HF-specific initial-point utility for UCC ansatzes that computes an all-zero parameter vector with the correct excitation-list length.
The HF initial-point utility must raise a clear error if neither an ansatz nor an excitation list has been provided before computation.
The HF initial-point utility must accept a grouped property containing electronic energy data and expose the Hartree-Fock reference energy when available.
VQEUCCFactory must default to an HF initial-point utility instead of leaving the initial point unset when the user does not provide one.

When VQEUCCFactory is used through GroundStateEigensolver with the default UCC workflow, the stored initial point must remain accessible as an initial-point utility and resolve to the all-zero UCC parameter vector.
Existing UCC-based ground-state solver behavior without the new HF initial-point path must keep working.

interface.Name: HFInitialPoint
interface.Description: Initial-point utility for UCC ansatzes that represents the Hartree-Fock starting point as an all-zero parameter vector.

interface.Name: HFInitialPoint.compute
interface.Description: Computes the Hartree-Fock initial point from a UCC ansatz or a pre-set excitation list and optional grouped-property metadata.

interface.Name: HFInitialPoint.to_numpy_array
interface.Description: Returns the computed all-zero UCC parameter vector, computing it on demand if needed.

interface.Name: VQEUCCFactory
interface.Input: constructor: quantum_instance, optimizer=None, initial_point=None, gradient=None, expectation=None, include_custom=False, ansatz=None, initial_state=None, callback=None, **kwargs
interface.Description: Factory for VQE UCC ground-state solvers whose default initial point must be a Hartree-Fock-compatible initial-point utility when none is provided by the user.

problem_statement: The lattice-model stack includes models such as the Ising model, but it lacks a Heisenberg model even though the Heisenberg Hamiltonian is a common spin-system model and generalizes several useful special cases. Users need a lattice-based Heisenberg model that can construct the corresponding spin Hamiltonian from a lattice, configurable axis couplings, and an external magnetic field.
requirements: A Heisenberg model must be available from the second-quantized lattice-model properties API.
The model must preserve and expose the lattice supplied at construction.
With default parameters on a two-node line lattice, the model must produce X, Y, and Z two-site spin interaction terms for the connected nodes.
The model must support arbitrary lattice connectivity, including triangular lattices, and produce same-axis two-site terms for every non-self edge.
The model must apply an external magnetic field across the X, Y, and Z axes as one-site spin terms on lattice self-edges.
The model must support per-axis coupling constants so that selected axes can be included or omitted.
The transverse-field Ising model must be reproducible as a special case by using only Z-axis coupling and an X-axis magnetic field.
Existing IsingModel lattice construction, uniform-parameter construction, parameter-matrix construction, coupling-matrix behavior, and second-quantized operator output must remain compatible.

interface.Name: HeisenbergModel
interface.Description: Represents a spin-1/2 Heisenberg lattice model using a lattice, per-axis coupling constants, and per-axis external magnetic-field coefficients.

interface.Name: HeisenbergModel.second_q_ops
interface.Description: Builds the Heisenberg Hamiltonian as a SpinOp, using same-axis two-site terms for lattice edges and one-site terms for nonzero external magnetic-field components on self-edges.

problem_statement: Qiskit Nature can represent Majorana operators, but it does not provide the ternary-tree qubit mapping described by Jiang, Kalev, Mruczkiewicz, and Neven. Users need a mapper that turns Majorana operators into SparsePauliOp qubit operators, supports configurable Pauli priority, and works consistently for single operators and mapped containers.
requirements: A TernaryTreeMapper must be available as a second-quantization mapper for MajoranaOp inputs.
The mapper must generate ternary-tree Pauli operators that satisfy the Majorana anticommutation relations.
Mapping a MajoranaOp must produce the expected SparsePauliOp for individual Majorana labels, parameterized coefficients, empty operators, constant operators, and register-length overrides.
Mapping lists or dictionaries of MajoranaOp instances must preserve the input container type and map each operator value.
The mapper must accept Pauli priority strings made from the six permutations of X, Y, and Z, and reject invalid priority strings with ValueError.
Existing Jordan-Wigner mapper behavior for FermionicOp inputs must remain compatible.

interface.Name: TernaryTreeMapper
interface.Description: Configures ternary-tree mapping for MajoranaOp inputs with a Pauli priority chosen from the six permutations of X, Y, and Z.

interface.Name: TernaryTreeMapper.map
interface.Description: Maps a MajoranaOp, list of MajoranaOp instances, or dictionary of MajoranaOp instances to SparsePauliOp qubit operators.

interface.Name: TernaryTreeMapper.pauli_table
interface.Description: Returns the ternary-tree Pauli lookup table used for compatibility with mode-based mapper behavior.

problem_statement: The refactored second-quantized operator stack has specialized coefficient containers for specific domains, but it lacks a general tensor container for arbitrary n-body operator coefficients. Users need a reusable PolynomialTensor container that can store keyed dense coefficient arrays, validate their dimensions, expose mapping-style access, and support basic linear and adjoint operations.
requirements: A PolynomialTensor class must be available from the second-quantized operators package.
PolynomialTensor construction must accept a mapping from string operator keys to numeric scalars or NumPy arrays together with a register length.
Construction must reject data whose array rank does not match the key length, whose array axes are not all the same length, or whose axis length does not match the provided register length.
PolynomialTensor instances must provide mapping-style key lookup, length, and iteration over stored coefficient keys.
Scalar multiplication must return a new PolynomialTensor with every stored coefficient scaled, and multiplying by another PolynomialTensor must raise TypeError.
Adding two PolynomialTensor instances with matching register length must combine common and unique keys into a new PolynomialTensor.
Adding an unsupported object must raise TypeError, and adding tensors with different register lengths must raise ValueError.
PolynomialTensor equality, conjugation, and transposition must operate on the stored coefficient arrays and preserve the register length.
Existing second-quantized operator arithmetic and adjoint behavior must remain compatible.

interface.Name: PolynomialTensor
interface.Description: Stores string-keyed numeric coefficient tensors for a fixed register length, validates key and tensor dimensions, supports mapping access, equality, scalar multiplication, addition, conjugation, and transposition.

interface.Name: PolynomialTensor.conjugate
interface.Description: Returns a PolynomialTensor containing the complex conjugate of each stored coefficient array.

interface.Name: PolynomialTensor.transpose
interface.Description: Returns a PolynomialTensor containing the transposed version of each stored coefficient array.

problem_statement: Second-quantized operator classes store sparse label-to-coefficient data and need a common base abstraction for behavior that is not specific to fermionic, vibrational, or spin semantics. Users need this shared sparse-label operator foundation to provide consistent storage, register-length handling, arithmetic, adjoint behavior, equality checks, mapping access, and copy semantics for concrete second-quantized operator implementations.
requirements: The second_q operator package must expose a SparseLabelOp base class for sparse second-quantized operators.
SparseLabelOp instances must store string labels mapped to numeric coefficients and retain a register length supplied at construction.
Construction must copy input data by default and must be able to keep the original mapping by reference when copy is disabled.
SparseLabelOp subclasses must support addition with other sparse-label operators by combining matching coefficients, preserving unique labels, and using the larger register length.
SparseLabelOp subclasses must support scalar multiplication by numeric values and reject unsupported scalar types with TypeError.
SparseLabelOp subclasses must support conjugation and adjoint behavior, with adjoint using the subclass transpose implementation followed by complex conjugation.
SparseLabelOp instances must support exact equality and tolerance-based equivalence checks over register length, labels, and coefficients.
SparseLabelOp instances must behave like a read-only mapping for key lookup, iteration over labels, and length.

interface.Name: SparseLabelOp
interface.Description: Abstract base class for sparse second-quantized operators backed by a mapping from string labels to numeric coefficients, exposing register length and read-only mapping behavior.

interface.Name: SparseLabelOp.register_length
interface.Description: Returns the register length stored on the operator.

interface.Name: SparseLabelOp._add
interface.Description: Combines two SparseLabelOp-compatible operands by adding coefficients for shared labels, preserving labels unique to the right operand, and returning a new instance with the maximum register length.

interface.Name: SparseLabelOp._multiply
interface.Description: Returns a new operator whose coefficients are multiplied by a numeric scalar and raises TypeError for unsupported scalar types.

interface.Name: SparseLabelOp.conjugate
interface.Description: Returns a new operator with each coefficient complex-conjugated while preserving register length.

interface.Name: SparseLabelOp.transpose
interface.Description: Abstract method implemented by subclasses to return the transposed sparse-label operator.

interface.Name: SparseLabelOp.equiv
interface.Description: Checks whether another SparseLabelOp has the same register length and labels with coefficient values equal within the operator tolerances.

interface.Name: SparseLabelOp.__eq__
interface.Description: Checks exact SparseLabelOp equality over type compatibility, register length, labels, and coefficient values.

interface.Name: SparseLabelOp.__getitem__
interface.Description: Returns the coefficient stored for a string label.

interface.Name: SparseLabelOp.__iter__
interface.Description: Iterates over the operator labels.

interface.Name: SparseLabelOp.__len__
interface.Description: Returns the number of labels stored in the operator.

problem_statement: BOPESSampler can sample potential energy surfaces with ground-state solvers, but it cannot consume excited-state solvers and return multiple energy curves for the same molecular geometry points. Users need BOPESSampler to work with excited-state solver workflows so they can sample ground and excited electronic-state energies across a potential energy surface.
requirements: BOPESSampler must accept an excited-state solver in the same sampling workflow used for ground-state solvers.
Sampling with an excited-state solver must evaluate each requested geometry point and return the sampled points unchanged.
The sampled energies must preserve the multiple electronic-state energies produced by the excited-state solver for each geometry point.
Existing BOPESSampler behavior for ground-state NumPyMinimumEigensolver workflows and Morse-potential fitting must remain compatible.

interface.Name: BOPESSampler
interface.Description: Configures potential-energy-surface sampling with either ground-state or excited-state solver workflows.

interface.Name: BOPESSampler.sample
interface.Description: Samples the configured solver at each geometry point and returns points, energies, and raw solver results.

interface.Name: BOPESSamplerResult
interface.Description: Stores sampled geometry points and scalar or multi-state energy values from BOPESSampler.

problem_statement: Spin-operator workflows are missing a logarithmic local encoding mapper. Users should be able to convert SpinOp instances into qubit operators with a dedicated LogarithmicMapper, including configurable embedding behavior for spins whose local Hilbert space does not exactly fill a power-of-two qubit register.
requirements: The repository must expose a LogarithmicMapper from qiskit_nature.mappers.second_quantization for mapping SpinOp instances to qubit operators.
LogarithmicMapper must map SpinOp inputs to PauliSumOp outputs using the logarithmic spin-to-qubit encoding across the dedicated single-spin and multi-spin cases covered by the mapper tests.
LogarithmicMapper must support configurable padding for embedded spin matrices when the local spin dimension is smaller than the allocated qubit space.
LogarithmicMapper must support choosing whether embedded matrices are placed in the upper or lower diagonal block of the larger qubit-space matrix.
Existing LinearMapper spin-to-qubit mapping behavior must remain compatible.

interface.Name: LogarithmicMapper
interface.Input: constructor: padding: float = 1, embed_upper: bool = True
interface.Description: Constructs a logarithmic spin-to-qubit mapper with configurable padding and upper-vs-lower embedding behavior.

interface.Name: LogarithmicMapper.map
interface.Description: Maps a SpinOp into a qubit operator using the logarithmic encoding.

problem_statement: Second-quantized operators can be compared exactly, but users do not have a simple operator-level helper for approximate equality when coefficients differ only within numerical tolerance. This makes it awkward to compare constructed operators in tests or numerical workflows, especially across different concrete second-quantized operator subclasses.
requirements: Second-quantized operators must provide an approximate-equality helper that compares two operators of the same concrete type.
The helper must return false when one operator contains terms or coefficients that are not equal to the other within the active tolerance.
The helper must return true when matching terms differ only within an explicitly supplied absolute tolerance.
When no tolerance is supplied, the helper must use the operator's default absolute tolerance.
Comparing against an object of an unsupported type must raise a TypeError whose message identifies the unsupported operand type.
Existing hermiticity and simplification behavior for the affected operator classes must remain compatible.

interface.Name: SecondQuantizedOp.equiv
interface.Description: Checks whether another operator of the same concrete SecondQuantizedOp type is approximately equal to this operator under the given absolute tolerance, using the operator default tolerance when none is supplied, and raises TypeError with a message identifying the unsupported operand type.

problem_statement: Qiskit Nature has second-quantized format support for QCSchema, but FCIDump parsing and export are not available through the same format layer. Users need FCIDump quantum-chemistry integral files to be represented as a structured format object, read from disk, written back to disk, and translated into an electronic-structure problem that can be solved by the existing second-quantized ground-state workflow.
requirements: Provide an FCIDump format object that stores one- and two-electron integral tensors, optional beta-spin tensors, electron count, orbital count, multiplicity, constant energy, orbital symmetries, and wave-function symmetry.
Parse restricted and unrestricted FCIDump files into the format object, including alpha, beta, and beta-alpha integral data.
Write FCIDump objects back to FCIDump text files while preserving header metadata and integral values needed for round-trip checks.

Translate an FCIDump object into an electronic-structure problem with ElectronicEnergy, ParticleNumber, Magnetization, AngularMomentum, and ElectronicDipoleMoment-compatible property behavior where applicable.
Allow FCIDump-backed electronic-structure problems to run through GroundStateEigensolver with a Jordan-Wigner qubit converter.
Keep existing QCSchema format JSON and legacy HDF5 behavior working.

interface.Name: FCIDump
interface.Input: constructor: hij, hijkl, hij_b=None, hijkl_ba=None, hijkl_bb=None, multiplicity, num_electrons, num_orbitals, constant_energy=None, orbsym=None, isym=1
interface.Description: Structured representation of FCIDump one- and two-electron integral data and metadata.

interface.Name: FCIDump.from_file
interface.Description: Reads an FCIDump file from disk and returns a populated FCIDump object.

interface.Name: FCIDump.to_file
interface.Description: Writes the FCIDump object to a text FCIDump file.

interface.Name: fcidump_to_problem
interface.Description: Converts FCIDump integral data into an electronic-structure problem for second-quantized workflows.

problem_statement: Qiskit Nature can model several second-quantized operator families independently, but it does not provide a first-class way to represent and map composite systems that combine multiple local Hilbert-space operator types. Users need mixed-particle operators and a mapper that can dispatch each component to the appropriate underlying mapper and combine the mapped qubit registers.
requirements: A mixed second-quantized operator must be available for representing weighted products of component operators over named Hilbert-space registers.

Mixed operators must support scalar multiplication and division, addition and subtraction across same or different register keys, unary negation, and composition across same or different register keys.
A mixed mapper must map MixedOp inputs by dispatching each component operator to the mapper associated with its register type and composing the resulting qubit operators in register order.
MixedMapper.map must preserve the container type when mapping lists or dictionaries of MixedOp instances.
MixedMapper construction must reject configurations that contain more than one fermionic register type.
Existing fermionic operator arithmetic and Jordan-Wigner mapping behavior must remain compatible.

interface.Name: MixedOp
interface.Description: Represents weighted products of component second-quantized operators over one or more named Hilbert-space registers.

interface.Name: MixedOp.compose
interface.Description: Composes mixed operators and combines register keys in order.

interface.Name: MixedMapper
interface.Description: Configures mapper dispatch for named Hilbert-space registers and validates supported register combinations.

interface.Name: MixedMapper.map
interface.Description: Maps MixedOp instances, lists, or dictionaries to qubit operators while preserving list and dictionary containers.

problem_statement: Second-quantized sparse-label operators currently assume numeric coefficients. Users need these operators to accept qiskit circuit Parameters and ParameterExpressions as coefficients, preserve those symbols through algebraic operator operations, expose and assign stored parameters, and allow qubit mapping of parameterized fermionic operators.
requirements: SparseLabelOp-compatible operators must accept Parameter and ParameterExpression coefficients alongside numeric coefficients.
Scalar multiplication, scalar division, composition, powers, simplification, and normal ordering must preserve parameter expressions when operating on FermionicOp instances.

SparseLabelOp must expose whether it contains parameters, return its stored parameters, and support assigning parameters to numeric values or other parameter expressions without mutating the original operator.

SparseLabelOp and FermionicOp methods that rely on numerical comparison, norms, matrix conversion, or hermiticity checks must reject unbound parameterized operators with a clear parameter-related error instead of silently coercing symbols.
Coefficient chopping must ignore symbolic coefficients while continuing to chop small real and imaginary numeric parts.
JordanWignerMapper must map parameterized FermionicOp coefficients into object-typed SparsePauliOp coefficients without forcing symbols to complex values.
Existing second-quantized operator and mapper behavior in the same directories must remain compatible.

interface.Name: SparseLabelOp
interface.Description: Sparse labeled operator base class accepting numeric and parameter-expression coefficients while preserving label-to-coefficient mappings.

interface.Name: SparseLabelOp.is_parameterized
interface.Description: Returns whether any coefficient in the operator is a parameter expression.

interface.Name: SparseLabelOp.parameters
interface.Description: Returns the parameter-expression coefficients stored by the operator.
