interface.Description: Returns a same-type operator whose coefficients matching keys in the supplied mapping are replaced by the mapped values.

interface.Name: FermionicOp
interface.Description: Fermionic sparse-label operator supporting parameterized coefficients through scalar multiplication, scalar division, composition, powers, simplification, and normal ordering.

interface.Name: FermionicOp.to_matrix
interface.Description: Converts numeric fermionic operators to matrices and raises a parameter-related error for unbound parameterized operators.

interface.Name: FermionicOp.is_hermitian
interface.Description: Checks numeric fermionic-operator hermiticity and raises a parameter-related error when parameters are present.

interface.Name: JordanWignerMapper
interface.Description: Mapper whose map method must preserve parameterized FermionicOp coefficients in the resulting qubit operator.

problem_statement: QubitConverter can map second-quantized operators to qubit operators, but it does not yet support the reduction workflow users need for molecular problems. Conversions should be able to apply mapper-aware two-qubit reduction and optional Z2 symmetry tapering, and follow-up matched conversions should reuse the same reduction settings instead of forcing callers to rebuild that state by hand.
requirements: QubitConverter must support mapper-aware two-qubit reduction during conversion when the mapper allows it and particle counts are provided.
When two-qubit reduction is requested but particle counts are omitted, conversion must leave the mapped operator unreduced and keep the stored particle-count state unset.
QubitConverter must support Z2 symmetry tapering by accepting an explicit symmetry sector and returning the tapered qubit operator for that sector.
After a conversion establishes two-qubit reduction and-or Z2 tapering state, convert_match must apply the same stored reduction settings to subsequent matched conversions.
Changing the configured tapering sector must affect later conversions, and invalid tapering sector values or incompatible tapering-sector lengths must raise validation errors.
Existing Jordan-Wigner and Parity mapper behavior, including standard mapping output and mapper-level two-qubit-reduction capability reporting, must remain compatible.

interface.Name: QubitConverter
interface.Description: Constructs a second-quantized to qubit-operator converter with optional two-qubit reduction and Z2 tapering defaults.

interface.Name: QubitConverter.convert
interface.Description: Maps a second-quantized operator and applies configured two-qubit reduction and optional Z2 symmetry tapering.

interface.Name: QubitConverter.convert_match
interface.Description: Converts additional operators using the reducer and tapering state established by earlier conversions.

interface.Name: QubitConverter.two_qubit_reduction
interface.Description: Reports whether mapper-aware two-qubit reduction is enabled and accepts updated boolean settings.

interface.Name: QubitConverter.z2symmetry_reduction
interface.Description: Reports and validates the configured tapering sector used for Z2 symmetry reduction.

interface.Name: QubitConverter.num_particles
interface.Description: Returns the particle-count state stored from the latest conversion for later matched reductions.

interface.Name: QubitConverter.z2symmetries
interface.Description: Returns the symmetry information detected during conversion, including tapering values used by later matched conversions.

problem_statement: The active-space and freeze-core transformers can reduce full electronic-structure problems, but users cannot apply the same reductions directly to standalone electronic Hamiltonians outside a problem object. Users need a way to prepare the transformer with the total system information and then transform a Hamiltonian by itself.
requirements: ActiveSpaceTransformer must support preparing active-space state from total electron and orbital counts before transforming a standalone electronic Hamiltonian.
FreezeCoreTransformer must support preparing active-space state from molecular system information and total orbital count before transforming a standalone electronic Hamiltonian.
Calling standalone Hamiltonian transformation before the transformer has been prepared must raise a QiskitNatureError.
After preparation, standalone Hamiltonian transformation must return the same reduced electronic-energy data and inactive-energy constants as the corresponding problem-level transformation.

interface.Name: ActiveSpaceTransformer
interface.Description: Transformer configured for an active-space reduction and able to retain prepared active-space state for standalone Hamiltonian transformation.

interface.Name: ActiveSpaceTransformer.prepare_active_space
interface.Description: Prepares the active basis and density information needed before transforming an electronic Hamiltonian outside a problem instance.

interface.Name: ActiveSpaceTransformer.transform_hamiltonian
interface.Description: Transforms a supported standalone electronic Hamiltonian after active-space preparation and raises QiskitNatureError if preparation is missing.

interface.Name: FreezeCoreTransformer
interface.Description: Transformer configured for freeze-core reduction and able to retain prepared active-space state for standalone Hamiltonian transformation.

interface.Name: FreezeCoreTransformer.prepare_active_space
interface.Description: Prepares the active basis and density information needed before freeze-core transforming an electronic Hamiltonian outside a problem instance.

interface.Name: FreezeCoreTransformer.transform_hamiltonian
interface.Description: Transforms a supported standalone electronic Hamiltonian after freeze-core preparation and raises QiskitNatureError if preparation is missing.

problem_statement: SparseLabelOp instances do not currently have the commutator helper routines that users may know from Qiskit opflow. Users need second-quantized operators to support direct commutator, anti-commutator, and symmetric double-commutator utilities, with results simplified consistently and a way to identify zero sparse-label operators.
requirements: The second_q operator package must provide commutator, anti-commutator, and double_commutator utilities for SparseLabelOp-compatible operands.
The commutator utility must compute AB - BA and return a simplified SparseLabelOp result.
The anti_commutator utility must compute AB + BA and return a simplified SparseLabelOp result.
The double_commutator utility must compute the symmetric double-commutator expression for three operands and support both sign conventions.
SparseLabelOp instances must expose an is_zero check that treats empty operators and coefficients within a tolerance as zero.
Existing second-quantized operator behavior in the same operators package must remain compatible.

interface.Name: commutator
interface.Description: Computes AB - BA for two SparseLabelOp-compatible operands and returns the simplified result.

interface.Name: anti_commutator
interface.Description: Computes AB + BA for two SparseLabelOp-compatible operands and returns the simplified result.

interface.Name: double_commutator
interface.Description: Computes the symmetric double-commutator expression for three SparseLabelOp-compatible operands and returns the simplified result.

interface.Name: SparseLabelOp.is_zero
interface.Description: Returns whether the operator is empty or all stored coefficients are zero within the given tolerance, using the operator tolerance when no explicit tolerance is supplied.

problem_statement: SparseLabelOp currently provides utilities such as chopping small coefficients, but it does not provide a direct way to round operator coefficients. Users need a round utility on SparseLabelOp instances so approximate real or complex coefficients can be rounded to a chosen decimal precision while preserving the operator type and labels.
requirements: SparseLabelOp instances must expose a round operation that returns an operator of the same concrete type with the same labels.
Calling round without an explicit precision must round each coefficient to the nearest integer value.
Calling round with a decimal precision must round each real or complex coefficient to that many decimal places.
Rounding must work for coefficients with real parts, imaginary parts, and combined complex values.
Existing SparseLabelOp behavior unrelated to rounding must remain compatible with the other second-quantized operator tests.

interface.Name: SparseLabelOp
interface.Description: Base sparse labeled operator container whose concrete subclasses store label-to-coefficient mappings and support creating same-type transformed instances.

interface.Name: SparseLabelOp.round
interface.Description: Returns a same-type operator with every coefficient rounded to the requested decimal precision while preserving the labels.

problem_statement: QuadraticHamiltonian stores tensor-like coefficient data, but it does not participate in the arithmetic and representation behavior shared by PolynomialTensor-backed containers. Users need compatible QuadraticHamiltonian objects to combine cleanly, scale by numeric factors from either side, compare by value, and display their coefficient data in a reproducible constructor-style form.
requirements: QuadraticHamiltonian instances must support equality and addition or subtraction with other compatible QuadraticHamiltonian instances.
QuadraticHamiltonian instances must support scalar multiplication from either side.
Arithmetic operations must combine the Hermitian part, antisymmetric part, and constant consistently with the requested operation.

The string representation must expose the Hermitian part, antisymmetric part, constant, and number of modes in a reproducible QuadraticHamiltonian constructor-style form, preserving the standard NumPy array representation including whitespace, line breaks, and alignment.

interface.Name: QuadraticHamiltonian.__repr__
interface.Description: Returns a constructor-style representation containing coefficient arrays, constant, and num_modes while preserving the standard NumPy array representation including whitespace, line breaks, and alignment.

problem_statement: PolynomialTensor and the operator utilities built on top of it currently assume dense NumPy arrays. Users need these tensor containers and conversions to work with sparse-array inputs so large mostly-empty tensor data can be represented, transformed, ordered, and converted without first densifying it.
requirements: PolynomialTensor must accept sparse array values alongside scalar constants and dense arrays while preserving existing dense behavior.
PolynomialTensor must report whether its stored tensor values are sparse, dense, mixed, or empty, and it must support conversion between sparse and dense storage.
PolynomialTensor arithmetic, conjugation, transpose, composition, tensor expansion, and einsum operations must preserve correct results for sparse tensor values.
FermionicOp construction from a PolynomialTensor must work for both dense and sparse tensor values.
ElectronicIntegrals must preserve sparse PolynomialTensor values in its spin-sector accessors and einsum workflows, including alpha/beta ordering transformations.
Tensor-ordering utilities must support sparse two-body tensors and return results equivalent to the dense tensor-ordering behavior.

The sparse optional dependency must be detected through qiskit_nature.optionals and exposed as a public qiskit_nature.optionals.HAS_SPARSE module attribute, so test and library code can import/access that exact attribute without AttributeError and use it to guard sparse-specific behavior when the sparse package is installed.
Existing dense operator behavior must remain compatible for PolynomialTensor, ElectronicIntegrals, FermionicOp, SpinOp, and related operator tests.

problem_statement: The second-quantized Hartree-Fock and VSCF initial-state circuits are built eagerly, so they cannot be instantiated first and configured later like other Qiskit blueprint circuits. Users need these initial states to support lazy construction and attribute-based configuration while preserving the same prepared states as the existing eager constructors.
requirements: HartreeFock must behave as a BlueprintCircuit-compatible initial state that can be constructed without all configuration values and completed later through attributes.
VSCF must behave as a BlueprintCircuit-compatible initial state that can be constructed without all configuration values and completed later through attributes.
Setting HartreeFock configuration attributes must invalidate and rebuild the circuit so the final state matches the eager constructor for the same orbitals, particles, and qubit converter.
Setting VSCF configuration attributes must invalidate and rebuild the circuit so the final state matches the eager constructor for the same modals and qubit converter.
HartreeFock must report an unsupported Bravyi-Kitaev Super Fast mapper through NotImplementedError when the circuit is built.
Existing Hartree-Fock and VSCF bitstring helper behavior must remain compatible with the prepared-state circuits.

interface.Name: HartreeFock
interface.Description: Blueprint-compatible initial-state circuit whose num_spatial_orbitals, num_particles, and qubit_converter configuration can be supplied at construction time or later through attributes.

problem_statement: The second-quantized mapper stack provides mapper implementations using the repository's default spin-orbital ordering, but it does not provide a wrapper for interleaved spin ordering. Users need a mapper that can reuse an existing QubitMapper while reordering fermionic operators into interleaved alpha/beta spin-orbital order before mapping.
requirements: An InterleavedQubitMapper must be available through the public second-quantized mapper API.
The mapper must wrap an existing QubitMapper and delegate the final qubit mapping to that wrapped mapper.
Before delegation, it must reorder FermionicOp mode indices from blocked spin ordering into interleaved spin ordering.
The resulting mapped qubit operator must match the wrapped mapper's output for the interleaved operator.

interface.Name: InterleavedQubitMapper
interface.Description: Mapper wrapper that stores an underlying QubitMapper and maps fermionic operators after converting their mode ordering to interleaved spin order.

interface.Name: InterleavedQubitMapper.map
interface.Description: Maps fermionic operators through the interleaved-order wrapper and returns the wrapped mapper's qubit-operator result.

problem_statement: The second-quantized ElectronicDensity property needs more efficient and configurable reduced-density-matrix handling. Users should be able to initialize an electronic density without measuring or storing the two-body RDM when it is not needed, and generated auxiliary operators should avoid redundant spin-block entries while preserving correct interpretation of measured one- and two-body density results.
requirements: Allow ElectronicDensity.from_orbital_occupation to optionally omit two-body RDM data.
When two-body RDM data is omitted, construct an ElectronicDensity containing only valid one-body alpha and beta density blocks.
Generate second-quantized RDM auxiliary operators only for required alpha-alpha, beta-beta, and beta-alpha spin-block indices instead of all spin-orbital index combinations.
When two-body RDM data is present, preserve correct alpha, beta, and beta-alpha two-body density blocks.
Interpret evaluated RDM auxiliary values back into ElectronicDensity objects with the same spin-block semantics.
Keep neighboring second-quantized property operator generation behavior working.

interface.Description: Creates an electronic density from alpha and beta orbital occupations, optionally excluding two-body RDM terms.

interface.Name: ElectronicDensity.second_q_ops
interface.Description: Builds auxiliary RDM measurement operators for the density blocks represented by the object.

interface.Description: Reads evaluated RDM auxiliary operator values and stores the interpreted electronic density on the result.

problem_statement: The SUCCD ansatz can build the standard singlet-paired double-excitation pool, but it cannot reproduce the legacy succ_full-style mirrored excitation grouping. Users who need that mirrored pool have no supported way to request it through SUCCD. The repository should add a mirror setting so SUCCD can generate the mirrored singlet-double excitation structure while keeping the existing non-mirrored behavior unchanged.
requirements: SUCCD must accept a mirror setting that enables the legacy succ_full-style mirrored singlet-double excitation pool.
When mirror is enabled, SUCCD must group symmetrically mirrored double excitations under shared parameters instead of generating only the default non-mirrored pool.
The mirrored SUCCD excitation generation must work for the standard singlet-paired configuration, for generalized excitations, and when optional single excitations are included.

Existing SUCCD behavior without mirror enabled must remain compatible, including standard excitation generation, generalized excitation generation, optional singles handling, and non-singlet validation.

interface.Description: Constructs the singlet-paired UCCD ansatz and must expose a mirror option for the mirrored excitation pool.

problem_statement: PolynomialTensor supports dense tensor contractions and can store sparse tensor data, but sparse einsum operations are not handled through an implementation that preserves sparse inputs. Users working with sparse PolynomialTensor data need einsum-based transformations to operate without unnecessary densification when an optional sparse-capable contraction backend is available.
requirements: Einsum-based tensor contractions must support dense, sparse, and mixed dense/sparse polynomial tensor inputs.
When the optional opt_einsum dependency is available, sparse tensor contractions must preserve sparse data instead of forcing dense arrays.
When opt_einsum is unavailable, existing dense-compatible einsum behavior must continue to work.
The einsum result must remain numerically equivalent to the corresponding dense contraction for one-body and two-body tensor transformations.
The optional dependency availability check must integrate with the repository's optional-dependency mechanism.

interface.Description: Applies mapped einsum contractions across PolynomialTensor operands, supporting dense, sparse, and mixed operands, using sparse-aware contraction when available and skipping mapped contractions whose operand keys are absent.

problem_statement: The second-quantized lattice Hamiltonians module includes several common lattice classes but does not provide a hexagonal lattice. Users need a dedicated HexagonalLattice class that follows the existing lattice API and can construct hexagonal lattice graphs directly from row and column counts with configurable edge and onsite weights.
requirements: A dedicated HexagonalLattice must be available through the public second-quantized lattice API.
The lattice must create a two-dimensional hexagonal graph for the requested row and column dimensions.
Node count, node indexes, and weighted edge lists must follow the existing Lattice semantics.
Bulk edges and onsite self-loops must be represented with the configured weights.
The weighted adjacency matrix must follow the existing Hermitian edge-weight convention, including conjugate entries for reverse directions.

interface.Description: Lattice class representing a hexagonal lattice graph with configurable edge and onsite weights, exposing graph, num_nodes, node_indexes, weighted_edge_list, and Hermitian weighted adjacency behavior.

interface.Description: Returns the hexagonal lattice adjacency matrix using the existing Hermitian weighted-edge convention.

problem_statement: The second-quantized lattice Hamiltonians module includes common lattice classes but does not provide a Kagome lattice. Users need a dedicated KagomeLattice class that follows the existing lattice API and supports open, periodic, and mixed boundary conditions.
requirements: A dedicated KagomeLattice must be available through the public second-quantized lattice API.
The lattice must create a two-dimensional Kagome graph with three sites per unit cell for the requested row and column dimensions.
Node count, node indexes, and weighted edge lists must follow the existing Lattice semantics.
The lattice must support open, fully periodic, x-periodic, and y-periodic boundary conditions using the existing BoundaryCondition API.
Bulk edges, boundary edges, and onsite self-loops must be represented with the configured weights.
The weighted adjacency matrix must follow the existing Hermitian edge-weight convention, including conjugate entries for reverse directions.

interface.Name: KagomeLattice.to_adjacency_matrix
interface.Description: Returns the Kagome lattice adjacency matrix using the existing Hermitian weighted-edge convention.

problem_statement: The second-quantized operator stack supports fermionic, spin, and vibrational operators, but it does not provide a first-class bosonic operator or a boson-to-qubit mapper. Users who need to model bosonic creation and annihilation terms cannot express those operators with the same sparse-label algebra or map them into qubit operators through the existing mapper workflow. The repository should support bosonic operators and a linear bosonic mapper.
requirements: The new bosonic operator must represent weighted sums of bosonic creation and annihilation terms using sparse labels with mode indices.
Construction must support explicit mode counts, automatic mode-count inference, optional validation skipping, and optional by-reference storage of input data.
Invalid labels or labels whose indices exceed the declared mode count must raise the repository's standard validation error when validation is enabled.

The operator must preserve existing sparse-label operator semantics for scalar arithmetic, addition, subtraction, composition, tensoring, expansion, powers, adjoints, equivalence checks, and induced norms.
Normal ordering must apply bosonic commutation relations, while index ordering and simplification must produce equivalent canonical forms without fermionic sign changes.
The operator must support parameterized coefficients where existing sparse-label arithmetic supports them, and hermiticity checks must reject parameterized operators.
The operator must convert to and from structured term iterators and construct from polynomial tensor data whose keys contain bosonic creation and annihilation placeholders.
Mode-index permutation must return an equivalent operator over the same mode count with every term index remapped by the provided permutation.
The bosonic operator and the linear bosonic mapper must be available from the public second-quantized operators and mappers APIs.
The linear bosonic mapper must map BosonicOp creation, annihilation, number-like, repeated, and cross-mode terms to SparsePauliOp results for different maximum occupation values.
The linear bosonic mapper must reject the deprecated PauliSumOp output setting with a clear error.

problem_statement: The second-quantized mapper stack already supports parity mapping and the legacy QubitConverter can perform two-qubit reduction for parity-mapped electronic problems. However, the ParityMapper itself does not own that reduction, even though this hard-coded symmetry only applies to parity mapping. Users need to configure parity mapping with particle numbers directly on the mapper and obtain the reduced qubit operator through the standard mapper workflow.
requirements: ParityMapper must accept optional particle-number information at construction time and expose it as mutable mapper state.
When particle numbers are available, parity mapping must apply the built-in two-qubit reduction after producing the parity-mapped qubit operator.
When particle numbers are absent, parity mapping must preserve the existing unreduced mapping behavior.
The tapering values used by the reduction must be derived from the alpha and beta particle counts and must update when the mapper's particle numbers change.
Two-qubit reduction must be skipped with the existing warning behavior when the mapped operator is too small to reduce.
QubitConverter must interoperate with ParityMapper's mapper-level reduction without applying unintended reductions when converter-level two-qubit reduction is disabled.
QEOM and excited-state solver workflows must accept both direct mappers and QubitConverter instances, including a ParityMapper configured for two-qubit reduction.

interface.Description: Parity fermion-to-qubit mapper with optional mapper-level particle numbers that enable two-qubit reduction.

interface.Description: Converts second-quantized operators while respecting converter-level reduction settings and mapper-level ParityMapper state.

problem_statement: Qiskit Nature already supports several fermion-to-qubit mappings, but it still lacks Bravyi-Kitaev super-fast mapping for FermionicOp inputs. Users need a public BravyiKitaevSuperFastMapper that can map fermionic terms through the BKSF construction, expose the expected edge-operator behavior internally, and produce the correct qubit operator for representative molecular Hamiltonians such as H2.
requirements: Provide a public BravyiKitaevSuperFastMapper in the second-quantization mapper package.
BravyiKitaevSuperFastMapper must accept FermionicOp input and return the corresponding qubit operator in the BKSF encoding.
The BKSF implementation must produce the expected edge operators for the internal a_ij and b_i constructions on representative interaction graphs.
BKSF mapping from FermionicOp must correctly identify fermionic interaction edges needed by excitation terms.
Mapping a representative H2 FermionicOp Hamiltonian through BravyiKitaevSuperFastMapper must produce the expected qubit operator after simplification.
Existing BravyiKitaevMapper, JordanWignerMapper, and ParityMapper behavior must remain compatible.

interface.Name: BravyiKitaevSuperFastMapper
interface.Description: Maps FermionicOp instances to qubit operators using the Bravyi-Kitaev super-fast mapping.

interface.Name: BravyiKitaevSuperFastMapper.map
interface.Description: Returns the qubit-operator image of a FermionicOp under the BKSF mapping.

interface.Name: _edge_operator_bi
interface.Description: Builds the BKSF b_i edge operator for a mode index on the interaction graph.

interface.Name: _edge_operator_aij
interface.Description: Builds the BKSF a_ij edge operator for a pair of interacting modes.

problem_statement: CplexOptimizer could solve QuadraticProgram instances through CPLEX, but users could not pass CPLEX solver parameters such as optimality target, time limit, thread count, or random seed through the optimizer API. This made it awkward to handle non-convex quadratic programs and warm-start workflows that require CPLEX options. The optimizer also assumed that CPLEX always returned a solution, instead of producing a structured failure result when no solution was found.
requirements: Extend CplexOptimizer so users can provide CPLEX parameters as a dictionary through the public optimizer API.
Store and expose the CPLEX parameter dictionary through a cplex_parameters property with a setter.
Pass the configured cplex_parameters into docplex.mp.model.Model.solve when solving a QuadraticProgram.
Continue respecting the disp flag by forwarding it as log_output to the DOcplex solve call.
When CPLEX returns no solution, return an OptimizationResult with zero-valued variables, an objective value evaluated at that fallback point, FAILURE status, and raw_results set to None.
When CPLEX returns a solution, preserve the existing OptimizationResult behavior, including objective value, variable values, feasibility-derived status, and raw solver result.
Keep CplexOptimizer unavailable with a MissingOptionalLibraryError when the cplex package is not installed.
Add tests that exercise normal CPLEX solving and no-solution handling through cplex_parameters.

interface.Name: CplexOptimizer
interface.Input: constructor: disp: bool = False, cplex_parameters: dict[str, Any] | None = None
interface.Description: OptimizationAlgorithm wrapper around CPLEX with configurable solver parameters.

interface.Name: CplexOptimizer.solve
interface.Description: Solves a quadratic program with DOcplex/CPLEX, forwarding display and CPLEX parameter settings and returning a structured failure result if no solution is found.

problem_statement: The DOcplex translator rejects DOcplex indicator constraints, so models that use conditional linear constraints cannot be imported into Qiskit Optimization through the translator. Users need indicator constraints to be translated into equivalent linear big-M constraints while preserving ordinary variable, objective, and constraint translation behavior.
requirements: Support docplex.mp.constr.IndicatorConstraint in the DOcplex-to-QuadraticProgram translator.
Translate indicator constraints into one or more linear constraints using a big-M formulation based on variable bounds when no explicit big-M value is supplied.
Accept an explicit indicator_big_m value and use it instead of automatically derived bounds when translating indicator constraints.
Handle active values 0 and 1 for indicator constraints.
Handle <=, >=, and == indicator linear constraints; equality indicators must become paired <= and >= linear constraints with stable names.
Preserve translated linear coefficients, senses, right-hand sides, and constraint names for the generated QuadraticProgram constraints.
Continue to reject unsupported DOcplex features such as equivalence, not-equal, logical, piecewise-linear, lazy, user-cut, SOS, and unsupported variable types.

interface.Name: from_docplex_mp
interface.Input: model: docplex.mp.model.Model, indicator_big_m: float | None = None
interface.Description: Translates a DOcplex model, including supported indicator constraints, into a QuadraticProgram.

problem_statement: Converting linear inequalities to QUBO currently goes through slack variables and equality penalties even for common binary-constraint patterns that can be represented directly as quadratic penalty terms. Users need a converter that recognizes those special linear inequality forms, removes the matching constraints, and adds the correct penalty terms to the objective while leaving non-matching constraints unchanged.
requirements: Add a LinearInequalityToPenalty converter that is importable from qiskit_optimization.converters.
For binary constraints of the form x <= y and x >= y, convert the inequality into the corresponding quadratic penalty without introducing slack variables.
For binary constraints of the form sum(x_i) <= 1 and sum(x_i) >= n - 1, convert the inequality into pairwise quadratic penalty terms without introducing slack variables.
Apply penalty terms with the correct sign for both minimization and maximization objectives, preserving existing objective constant, linear, and quadratic terms.
Leave linear or quadratic constraints that do not match the supported special patterns in the converted problem.

Automatically compute a penalty value from objective bounds when no penalty is supplied, and fall back to a default value when fractional constraint coefficients make automatic calculation unreliable.
Expose a mutable penalty setting and remember the penalty value used during conversion.
QuadraticProgramToQubo must include the new linear-inequality-to-penalty conversion in its default converter pipeline.
Interpreting a converted solution must return the original variable vector and reject vectors with the wrong length using QiskitOptimizationError.

interface.Name: LinearInequalityToPenalty
interface.Description: QuadraticProgramConverter that converts supported binary linear inequality patterns into objective penalty terms.

interface.Name: LinearInequalityToPenalty.convert
interface.Description: Returns a converted problem with matching special linear inequalities removed and represented as objective penalty terms.

interface.Name: LinearInequalityToPenalty.interpret
interface.Description: Returns the original variable vector and raises QiskitOptimizationError when the vector length does not match the source problem.

interface.Name: LinearInequalityToPenalty.penalty
interface.Input: get or set penalty: float | None
interface.Description: Gets or sets the penalty coefficient; setting None enables automatic penalty calculation on conversion.

interface.Name: LinearInequalityToPenalty._auto_define_penalty
interface.Description: Computes the automatic penalty coefficient from objective bounds or returns the default fallback when fractional constraint coefficients are present.

interface.Name: QuadraticProgramToQubo
interface.Description: Default QUBO converter whose conversion pipeline includes LinearInequalityToPenalty.

interface.Name: QuadraticProgramToQubo.convert
interface.Description: Converts a QuadraticProgram to QUBO using the default converter pipeline, including special linear inequality penalty conversion.

problem_statement: Optimization algorithms and QUBO conversion handled maximization problems by scattered local sign-flipping logic. Users need a reusable converter that turns maximization QuadraticProgram instances into minimization form, plugs into the default QUBO conversion flow, and lets algorithms consistently interpret solutions back in the original objective sense.
requirements: Add a MaximizeToMinimize converter that is importable from qiskit_optimization.converters.
When converting a maximization QuadraticProgram, return a minimization problem with objective constant, linear coefficients, and quadratic coefficients sign-flipped.
When converting an already-minimizing QuadraticProgram, preserve its objective sense and objective values.
QuadraticProgramToQubo must include maximization-to-minimization conversion in its default conversion pipeline and preserve interpretation back to original variables.

MinimumEigenOptimizer must accept the maximization-to-minimization converter in its converter pipeline and report interpreted samples, raw samples, objective values, and statuses consistently with the original problem sense.
GroverOptimizer must work with maximization problems through the converter pipeline while reporting final objective values in the original problem sense.
Existing optimization algorithms in the same directory must remain compatible.

interface.Name: MaximizeToMinimize
interface.Description: QuadraticProgramConverter that converts maximization problems into minimization problems and leaves minimization problems unchanged.

interface.Name: MaximizeToMinimize.convert
interface.Description: Returns a minimization-form QuadraticProgram, sign-flipping the objective only when the source problem is maximization.

interface.Name: MaximizeToMinimize.interpret
interface.Description: Returns the solution vector for the original problem after conversion.

interface.Name: QuadraticProgramToQubo
interface.Description: Default QUBO converter whose conversion pipeline includes MaximizeToMinimize and whose interpret method composes the converter interpretations.

interface.Name: MinimumEigenOptimizer
interface.Input: constructor: min_eigen_solver, penalty: float | None = None, converters=None
interface.Description: Optimizer that solves converted QUBO problems with a minimum eigensolver and interprets samples and objective values back to the original problem.

interface.Name: MinimumEigenOptimizer.solve
interface.Description: Solves a QuadraticProgram through the converter pipeline and exposes interpreted solution samples together with raw converted-problem samples.

interface.Name: GroverOptimizer
interface.Input: constructor: num_value_qubits, num_iterations=3, converters=None, penalty=None, quantum_instance=None
interface.Description: Optimizer that solves converted minimization QUBO problems and interprets results back to the original problem sense.

interface.Name: GroverOptimizer.solve
interface.Description: Solves a QuadraticProgram through the converter pipeline and reports samples and objective values consistently with the original problem.

problem_statement: Qiskit Optimization optimizers were still tied to legacy QuantumInstance and opflow-style result handling. Users needed primitives-based workflows to work with the optimization algorithms, including QAOA-style sampling minimum eigensolvers, sampler-backed Grover optimization, and a common helper for extracting the most likely bit string from sampled or statevector results.
requirements: Allow MinimumEigenOptimizer to solve problems with primitive-based sampling minimum eigensolvers such as QAOA using a Sampler.
Convert primitive quasi-distribution outputs into SolutionSample and raw sample records with valid bit-string ordering, probabilities, objective values, and statuses.
Allow GroverOptimizer to run with a Sampler instead of requiring a legacy QuantumInstance.
Provide OptimizationApplication.sample_most_likely for statevectors, opflow StateFn values, dictionaries of sampled bit strings, and QuasiDistribution values.
Keep existing NumPyMinimumEigensolver behavior and converter-list behavior working.

interface.Name: MinimumEigenOptimizer
interface.Input: constructor: min_eigen_solver, penalty: float | None = None, converters = None, filter_criterion = None
interface.Description: Accepts both legacy and primitive-based minimum eigensolver objects and prepares optimization results from their outputs.

interface.Name: MinimumEigenOptimizer.solve
interface.Description: Solves converted binary optimization problems with supported minimum eigensolvers and returns interpreted samples and raw samples.

interface.Name: GroverOptimizer
interface.Input: constructor: num_value_qubits: int, num_iterations: int = 3, converters = None, penalty: float | None = None, quantum_instance = None, sampler = None
interface.Description: Supports either the legacy quantum_instance path or a primitives Sampler path for Grover-based optimization.

interface.Name: GroverOptimizer.solve
interface.Description: Runs Grover optimization and returns optimization samples when using sampler-backed execution.

interface.Name: OptimizationApplication.sample_most_likely
interface.Description: Extracts the most likely binary sample from statevector-like and quasi-distribution-like inputs.

problem_statement: Qiskit Optimization's Ising translators still depended on the legacy opflow operator stack. Users needed the package to translate binary QuadraticProgram instances to modern SparsePauliOp operators and to rebuild quadratic programs from SparsePauliOp, Pauli, and related quantum_info operators while keeping the old opflow behavior available during migration.
requirements: Allow to_ising to return either legacy opflow operators or quantum_info operators, with SparsePauliOp support available through an explicit option.
Allow from_ising to accept SparsePauliOp and Pauli-style quantum_info operators as well as existing opflow operators.
Preserve the numeric operator coefficients, offsets, objective constants, linear terms, and quadratic terms for minimization and maximization conversions.
Reject invalid SparsePauliOp inputs containing X or Y terms, terms with more than two Z operators, or imaginary coefficients with the existing QiskitOptimizationError behavior.
Support constant-only and empty QuadraticProgram instances when converting to Ising form.
Keep opflow compatibility available and emit migration warnings when callers rely on default or legacy opflow behavior.

interface.Name: to_ising
interface.Input: quad_prog: QuadraticProgram, opflow: bool | None = None
interface.Description: Converts a binary QuadraticProgram to an Ising operator and offset, returning SparsePauliOp-compatible quantum_info operators when opflow is false and legacy opflow operators when opflow is true or defaulted; defaulted or legacy opflow paths must emit UserWarning migration warnings.

interface.Name: from_ising
interface.Input: qubit_op: OperatorBase | BaseOperator, offset: float = 0.0, linear: bool = False
interface.Description: Builds a QuadraticProgram from supported opflow or quantum_info Ising operators while preserving linear/quadratic interpretation and validation errors.

interface.Name: QuadraticProgram.to_ising
interface.Description: Delegates to the translator and exposes the same opflow selection behavior from QuadraticProgram instances, including UserWarning migration warnings for defaulted or legacy opflow paths.

interface.Name: QuadraticProgram.from_ising
interface.Input: qubit_op: OperatorBase | BaseOperator, offset: float = 0.0, linear: bool = False
interface.Description: Populates the current QuadraticProgram from supported opflow or quantum_info Ising operators.

problem_statement: Qiskit Optimization did not include Quantum Random Access Optimization (QRAO), so users could not encode binary quadratic optimization problems into quantum random access code relaxations, solve the relaxed Hamiltonian with primitive-based minimum eigensolvers, and round the relaxed result back to classical bit-string solutions from inside the package. The QRAO prototype needed to be integrated into the optimization algorithm stack with Qiskit primitives, SparsePauliOp-based operators, rounding schemes, tests, and public exports.
requirements: Add a qiskit_optimization.algorithms.qrao module that exposes QRAO encoding, rounding, and optimizer classes through the package public API.

Implement QuantumRandomAccessEncoding for 1, 2, and 3 variables per qubit, including QRAC operator assignment, encoded SparsePauliOp construction, offsets, compression metrics, and state preparation circuits.
Reject unsupported encodings and unsupported optimization problems with clear errors.
Provide a commutation verifier that checks encoded objective values against original quadratic-program objective values.
Implement SemideterministicRounding and MagicRounding to convert relaxed expectation values or sampled QRAC measurements into SolutionSample objects.
Implement QuantumRandomAccessOptimizer with solve_relaxed and solve workflows that accept auxiliary-operator-capable minimum eigensolvers such as NumPyMinimumEigensolver and VQE.
Return a QuantumRandomAccessOptimizationResult containing rounded samples, relaxed objective data, the relaxed eigensolver result, and rounding metadata.
Use Qiskit primitives and SparsePauliOp rather than legacy quantum-instance or opflow APIs.

interface.Name: QuantumRandomAccessEncoding
interface.Description: Encodes a binary QuadraticProgram into a QRAC-backed SparsePauliOp relaxation, exposing the encoded problem, qubit operator, offset, variable count, and variable-to-Pauli mapping metadata.

interface.Name: QuantumRandomAccessEncoding.encode
interface.Description: Builds the qubit operator, offset, and variable-to-Pauli mapping for the relaxed problem.

interface.Name: QuantumRandomAccessEncoding.state_preparation_circuit
interface.Description: Builds the QRAC state preparation circuit for a classical bit string under the encoded variable assignment.

interface.Name: EncodingCommutationVerifier.__len__
interface.Description: Returns the number of encoded bit-string assignments covered by the verifier.

interface.Name: EncodingCommutationVerifier.__iter__
interface.Description: Iterates over encoded bit strings together with original and encoded objective values.

interface.Description: Context object passed to QRAO rounding schemes.

interface.Name: RoundingResult
interface.Input: constructor: expectation_values: list[complex] | None, samples: list[SolutionSample], bases: np.ndarray | None = None, basis_shots: np.ndarray | None = None, basis_counts: list[dict[str, int]] | None = None
interface.Description: Result object returned by QRAO rounding schemes.

interface.Name: MagicRounding

interface.Description: Samples QRAC measurement bases and rounds measurement outcomes into classical optimization samples.

interface.Name: MagicRounding.round

interface.Name: MagicRounding._make_circuits

interface.Description: Builds QRAC measurement circuits for sampled bases and validates the variables-per-qubit setting.

interface.Input: constructor: atol: float = 1e-8, seed: int | None = None
interface.Description: Rounds relaxed expectation values deterministically when signs are nonzero and randomly for ambiguous values.

interface.Name: SemideterministicRounding.round
interface.Description: Rounds a relaxed QRAO solution from expectation values without running additional quantum sampling.

interface.Description: Runs QRAO by encoding a quadratic program, solving the relaxed Hamiltonian, and rounding to classical solutions.

interface.Input: constructor: x: list[float] | np.ndarray, fval: float, variables: list[Variable], status: OptimizationResultStatus, samples: list[SolutionSample], encoding: QuantumRandomAccessEncoding, relaxed_fval: float, relaxed_result: MinimumEigensolverResult, rounding_result: RoundingResult
interface.Description: Optimization result returned by the full QRAO solve workflow, including rounded samples and relaxed-solver metadata.

problem_statement: The TSP application can model complete geometric traveling-salesman instances, but it assumes every pair of nodes is connected. Users who already have weighted NetworkX graphs cannot model sparse or otherwise custom TSP instances directly because missing edges are not represented as invalid transitions. The application should support arbitrary weighted graphs while preserving the existing complete-graph behavior.
requirements: The TSP application must accept weighted NetworkX graphs that are not complete.
The generated quadratic program must include binary variables for every node-position assignment.
Objective terms must use the weights of existing graph edges in both travel directions for an undirected graph.
Missing graph edges must be encoded as constraints that prevent consecutive positions from using those non-adjacent node pairs in either direction.
Existing node-visit and position-occupancy constraints must remain unchanged.
Interpreting a result must return the ordered node route, and the edge-list helper must return route edges in order.
Random geometric TSP instances and TSPLIB parsing must keep their existing complete-graph behavior.

interface.Name: Tsp
interface.Description: Traveling-salesman application backed by a weighted NetworkX graph, exposing the graph used by random and TSPLIB-created instances.

interface.Name: Tsp.to_quadratic_program
interface.Description: Builds a quadratic-program formulation of the graph-backed TSP instance.

interface.Name: Tsp.interpret
interface.Description: Converts an optimization result into the corresponding ordered route.

interface.Name: Tsp._edgelist
interface.Description: Returns the route edges in traversal order.

interface.Name: Tsp.create_random_instance
interface.Input: n: int, low: int = 0, high: int = 100, seed: int | None = None
interface.Description: Creates a random complete geometric TSP instance with weighted graph edges.

interface.Name: Tsp.parse_tsplib_format
interface.Description: Parses a TSPLIB file into a complete weighted TSP instance.

problem_statement: QuadraticProgram had built-in methods for translating to and from DOcplex models, but users needed a reusable translator interface that could live outside the core problem class. The optimization package should provide DOcplex MP translator functions that convert supported models both into and out of QuadraticProgram while rejecting unsupported DOcplex constructs with the package's optimization error.
requirements: Provide a qiskit_optimization.translators package that exposes DOcplex MP translator entry points.
Convert a DOcplex MP model with binary, integer, and continuous variables into an equivalent QuadraticProgram.
Convert QuadraticProgram objectives, linear constraints, and quadratic constraints to and from DOcplex MP while preserving names, bounds, senses, constants, linear terms, and quadratic terms.
Reject unsupported DOcplex MP constructs such as semi-integer variables, range constraints, indicator constraints, equivalence constraints, and not-equal constraints with QiskitOptimizationError.
Existing QuadraticProgram expression, constraint, objective, and variable behavior in the same directory must remain compatible.

interface.Name: from_docplex_mp
interface.Description: Translates a supported DOcplex MP model into an equivalent QuadraticProgram and raises QiskitOptimizationError for unsupported model elements.

interface.Name: to_docplex_mp
interface.Description: Translates a QuadraticProgram into an equivalent DOcplex MP model.

interface.Name: QuadraticProgram
interface.Description: Optimization problem container accepted by to_docplex_mp and returned by from_docplex_mp, preserving variables, objectives, and constraints in exported LP form.

interface.Name: QiskitOptimizationError
interface.Description: Error raised by from_docplex_mp for unsupported DOcplex MP model elements.

problem_statement: Qiskit Optimization users need native support for warm-start QAOA. The optimizer should be able to use a classical pre-solver or max-cut relaxation result to initialize QAOA with problem-dependent initial states and mixers, then return optimization results through the same result pathway as existing minimum-eigen optimizers.
requirements: Provide a warm-start QAOA optimizer that accepts a pre-solver, QAOA instance, relaxation mode, epsilon regularization, optional multiple initial solutions, optional warm-start factory, and optional aggregation strategy.
Use relaxed or pre-solved binary optimization results to construct valid warm-start initial variables, initial states, and mixer operators for QAOA.
Solve max-cut, constrained binary, and simple QUBO problems through the warm-start QAOA workflow and return interpreted optimization results with solution vectors and objective values.
Support aggregating multiple warm-start QAOA results when the pre-solver provides multiple initial solutions, using a callable aggregation strategy when supplied.
Keep existing minimum-eigen optimizer sample handling and SLSQP-based QUBO solving behavior working.

interface.Input: constructor: pre_solver, relax_for_pre_solver, qaoa, epsilon = 0.25, num_initial_solutions = 1, warm_start_factory = None, aggregator = None, penalty = None, converters = None
interface.Description: Optimizer that prepares warm-start QAOA runs from pre-solved optimization results and invokes a supplied callable aggregator when multiple warm-start results must be combined.

interface.Name: WarmStartQAOAOptimizer.solve
interface.Description: Solves an optimization problem by preparing warm-start QAOA circuits, optionally aggregating multiple warm-start results, and interpreting the resulting samples.

interface.Description: Creates warm-start initial variables, initial states, and mixer operators from relaxed binary solutions.

interface.Name: MeanAggregator
interface.Description: Callable aggregator that combines samples from multiple warm-start QAOA optimization results.

interface.Input: constructor: num_cuts: int, sort_cuts: bool = True, unique_cuts: bool = True, seed: int = 0
interface.Description: Produces max-cut candidate solutions that can be used as warm-start pre-solver results.

interface.Name: max_cut_qp
interface.Description: Builds a QuadraticProgram representation of a max-cut instance from an adjacency matrix.

problem_statement: Tangelo ansatz generators currently expect string-based reference states such as Hartree-Fock or zero state, which makes it awkward to use custom prepared reference circuits for nonstandard mappings or handcrafted initial states. The ansatz workflow needs to accept a Tangelo Circuit object as the reference state for HEA construction, preserve its gates as the initialization prefix, and avoid treating variational parameters from the supplied reference circuit as ansatz optimization variables.
requirements: HEA must accept a Tangelo Circuit object as its reference_state input.
When a Circuit reference state is provided, HEA must prepend an equivalent copy of that circuit to the constructed ansatz circuit.
Variational gates coming from the supplied reference circuit must be frozen so they do not remain variational ansatz parameters after the reference circuit is incorporated.
HEA must continue to support existing non-reference-circuit behavior for standard variational parameter handling and default Hartree-Fock based circuit construction.

interface.Name: HEA
interface.Input: constructor: molecule=None, mapping='jw', up_then_down=False, n_layers=2, rot_type='euler', n_qubits=None, n_electrons=None, spin=None, reference_state='HF'
interface.Description: Hardware-efficient ansatz generator supports either standard string reference states or a Tangelo Circuit object as the initialization circuit.

interface.Name: HEA.prepare_reference_state
interface.Description: Builds the reference state circuit for HEA and returns a fixed-parameter copy when the reference state is already provided as a Circuit.

interface.Name: Circuit.fix_variational_parameters
interface.Description: Converts all variational gates in the circuit into fixed gates so a reference circuit can be reused as a non-variational initialization state.

problem_statement: Tangelo can translate abstract circuits to Qiskit, but it still rejects multi-controlled controlled-rotation style gates even though Qiskit now supports native multi-controlled variants for these operations. Users working with Tangelo circuits that contain multi-controlled CRX, CRY, CRZ, or phase-style controlled rotations need the Qiskit translator to emit the equivalent native Qiskit circuit instead of raising an unsupported multi-control error.
requirements: Translating a Tangelo circuit to the qiskit backend must support multi-controlled CRX, CRY, CRZ, and controlled phase style rotation gates when the gate control field contains multiple qubits.
For these supported multi-controlled rotation and phase gates, the translated qiskit circuit must use the corresponding native multi-controlled Qiskit gate behavior rather than rejecting the gate.
Existing qiskit translation behavior for single-control gates and for unsupported multi-controlled gate families must remain unchanged.

interface.Name: translate_circuit
interface.Description: Dispatches Tangelo circuit translation to the requested backend-specific translator.

interface.Name: translate_c_to_qiskit
interface.Description: Translates a Tangelo abstract circuit into an equivalent qiskit circuit, including supported multi-controlled controlled-rotation and phase gates.

interface.Name: get_qiskit_gates
interface.Description: Provides the Tangelo-to-Qiskit gate mapping used by qiskit circuit translation.
